title: ECOM Build and Deploy Pipeline
content: Automated CI/CD pipeline for ECOM services. Build stage compiles code, runs unit tests, and performs static code analysis. Deploy stage includes deployment to DEV environment, automated integration tests, and optional deployment to UAT. Uses Docker containers for consistent deployment across environments. Pipeline triggers on Git commits to main branch.

title: Kenan Deployment Pipeline
content: Deployment pipeline for Kenan system. Stages include database migration scripts validation, application build with Oracle dependencies, unit and integration testing, and staged deployment to UAT environment. Manual approval required before production deployment. Includes automated rollback capability if health checks fail.

title: ESOM Integration Test Pipeline
content: End-to-end integration testing pipeline for ESOM. Tests complete provisioning workflows including integration with ECOM, Kenan, and NetworkProvisioningService. Uses test data fixtures and mocked external services. Validates workflow state transitions, error handling, and rollback mechanisms. Runs nightly and on-demand.

title: ECOM Service Architecture
content: The ECOM (E-Commerce) service is built on a microservices architecture. It consists of multiple components: OrderService handles order processing, PaymentService manages payment transactions, and InventoryService tracks product availability. The services communicate via Message Queue and store data in MongoDB. The API Gateway routes external requests to appropriate services.

title: Kenan System Documentation
content: Kenan is the billing and customer management system. It includes BillingEngine for invoice generation, CustomerService for account management, and ReportingService for analytics. Kenan integrates with external payment gateways and uses Oracle database for persistent storage. The system processes billing cycles monthly and supports real-time rating and charging.

title: ESOM Integration Guide
content: ESOM (Enterprise Service Order Management) orchestrates service provisioning across multiple systems. It connects to Kenan for billing setup, ECOM for e-commerce integration, and NetworkProvisioningService for network activation. ESOM uses workflow engine to manage complex provisioning flows and maintains state in PostgreSQL database. Integration with external systems uses REST APIs and message queues.

title: Enterprise_ECOM_FrontEnd_Operations_Guide.docx - SSO and Session Management
content: SSO and Session Management ECOM SSO and Session Management For a user who only can access ECOM module, or only work on other system in ECOM solution landscape, one (1) active session is allowed. If the user login again from different PC / new tab in the same browser, the previous session should be automatic expired, ECOM will redirect the latest session to login page. If user has permission to access both ECOM and the other system in ECOM landscape and decide to access both concurrently, he/she just needs to login once. The user will have one (1) active session for ECOM, one (1) active session for the other system. In other words, the user can work on ECOM and the other system concurrently on same PC and browser. After login either system, to access another module will be via ECOM main page. ECOM will terminate session if the user has been inactive for a specifiable period of time (configurable). User would be prompted X (to be determined) mins before session timeout System will prompt user to “save” the work done. Unsaved work will be deleted when time-out happens The user will be required to logon again The ECOM will prevent replay of authenticated sessions, in other words, timeout and logout authentication sessions cannot be re-used. Integration with CRM via LIC and SSO CRM will be used for case and interaction management. CRM will launch ECOM Front End to access ECOM application directly with SSO. CRM will control which ECOM screen would be launched, and pass in necessary parameters with ECOM URL for ECOM to retrieve relevant info and show it on screen. ECOM will support CRM LIC and SSO: CRM users will be assigned a dealer code Users will login CES CRM and will be authenticated using ASM integrated with VAD User will launch ECOM where user ID and security token will be passed to ECOM by Amdocs CRM ECOM will validate security token from ASM Authenticated user will access ECOM or other system in ECOM landscape

title: Enterprise_ECOM_FrontEnd_Operations_Guide.docx - Authentication and Authorization
content: Authentication and Authorization Authentication ECOM front-end pass username and password to Front End Controller Controller will integrate with VAD to authenticate the user Logout user will be redirect to login page. Session will be inactive and security token will expire Authorization Each user is assigned a dealer code. all backroom officer will share the same dealer code For authenticated users, ECOM will based on the username and dealer code mapping to decide launching screen via hyperlink If username is mapped to backroom dealer code, ECOM Front End main page will be launched If username is mapped to other system in ECOM, its Front-End main page will be launched If username is mapped to both backroom dealer code and SME Retail dealer code, user needs to choose one of ECOM modules, the corresponding main page will be launched User privileges and access level control in ECOM and other system in ECOM will leverage existing mechanism. For instance, back dated CRD restriction will reuse existing control. IConnect Framework ITrust will be used to manage application security. It will auto validation user status and privilege ECOM will control the URL security by ITrust. For instance, it will redirect to login page when user logout and try to access system again ECOM individual pages are deep linkable via the URLs and that URLs are unique with security control. Only authenticated and authorized user can access the pages/URLs The following diagram illustrate ECOM authentication and authorization mechanism. Figure 1 ECOM Authentication and Authorization Sequence Diagram ECOM Authentication and Authorization involves the following sequence of steps: Table 4: ECOM A&A Steps STEP DESCRIPTION 1.0 ECOM user request to access ECOM System 1.1 ECOM iTrust Framework will check if the request has token 1.2 If without token, the request will be redirect to login page 1.3 ECOM pass UID and password to VAD for authentication 1.4 VAD will authenticate the user against active directory 1.5 ECOM iTrust Framework will generate token for this user. The token will be injected to every restful request. userID is included in token. Token is encrypted and stored securely in client browser session storage 1.6 ECOM will authorize the user - the user has privilege to access ECOM 1.7 When user access ECOM backroom module, ECOM will pass UID to ECOM backend 1.8 ECOM module will conduct transaction level authorization 1.9 If the UID passes authorization, ECOM return the requested page to user 1.10 When user access other system in ECOM landscape, ECOM will pass UID to it 1.11 The system will conduct transaction level authorization 1.12 If pass authorization, ECOM return the requested page to user 2.0 Front end issues logout request 2.1 ECOM iTrust Framework will delete the token from session storage 2.2 ECOM application session will be expired

title: Enterprise_ECOM_FrontEnd_Operations_Guide.docx - High Level Architecture
content: High Level Architecture ECOM includes following functional components: Web Layer ECOM user will use web browser instead of thick client ECOM Front End is web responsive design Every page will have URL with security control It provides front-end users with familiar experiences including similar processes and screens with an up-dated look-and-feel Front-end gears up following technology to build highly user friendly, interactive and responsive user interface Angular Framework HTML 5 Bootstrap CSS Server Layer ECOM Server Layer contains the business logic that supports ECOM core functions. It includes Session Beans, Tasks and JPA Note: ECOM Backend solution detail refers to D2551-01 ECOM Backend High Level Solution Design Data Model design refers to D2604-01-ECOM Data Model High Level Solution Design The diagram below illustrates ECOM Front End high-level architecture. Figure 2 ECOM Front End Architecture Web Tier UI View UI View is a HTML5 page UI Template It is to control the look and feel of a Web page UI screen It is entire UI web page including router, data and other information FORM / JSON Object It contains form data passed from web page, e.g. customer name, customer type etc. Web Browser and Server layer Integration Web browser to server Augular6 framework will get Form Object and call restful API to send Form Object to server side. It is used Angular HTTP Client component implement it. Response from Server to web Angular framework will use http client component to call server restful API to retrieve data. Data model To-be data model will be same as existing java object that will be converted into typescript object Application Tier Service Proxy: expose RESTful APIs Session Bean: Uplift OP activity bean to EJB3 session bean; maintain context and provides exception handling; create, trigger and manage Tasks Tasks: Uplift OP tasks java class to manipulate Database: Invoke JPA (EJB3) or Directly interact with Database via JNDI name JPA: Uplift OP Entity Bean to JPA EJB3 for accessing, persisting, and managing data between Java objects / classes and Database JAM: Uplift OP backend JAM to handle logging, DB connection, code table (cache) and configuration file reading etc. Cache Server: store frequently queried data in a temporary memory The diagram below provides an overview of data flow between Front End and Backend. Figure 3 ECOM Backend Domain Object & Data Flow Submit Form / JSON Object: Form / JSON object from ECOM Front End will be submitted to Controller as request Controller (Service Proxy): It controls data flow and intercepts incoming requests Domain Object: It models and persists data object like Customer, Order, NPP etc. ECOM Service Layer: It concludes Session Beans, Tasks and JPA and interacts with Database, and populate data in Domain Object Controller passes Domain Object to ECOM Front End

title: Enterprise_ECOM_FrontEnd_Operations_Guide.docx - Solution Component Details
content: Solution Component Details 3.2.3.1 User Interface ECOM Front End leverages on HTML5, Angular6 and Bootstrap4 CSS3, which gear up to build highly user friendly, interactive and responsive user interface Bootstrap as very popular CSS framework provides a professional and consistent stylesheet across ECOM UIs, for typography, forms, buttons, navigation etc. Front End pages are using Client-Side Rendering and template to provide the dynamic content that is powered by iConnect framework. It redirects the request to a bare-bones HTML file, typescript will fetch data from server side and rendering the content to browser The template consists of responsive web page layout, style sheets etc., which can help accelerate the development of ECOM web application significantly Angular as client-side MVC framework controls screen navigation, conducts data binding, routing, fetching data from server etc. Angular will conduct screen level data validation 3.2.3.2 Controller Controller accepts GUI input and converts it to commands for the model or view It responds to the user input and performs interactions on the data model objects 3.2.3.3 Impact Analysis GUI Elements Existing OP UI elements and respective logic, e.g. combo box, will retain and being modernized with angular6. Data Object ECOM will uplift the existing swing screen data and component, replace them with HTML label. Angular6 framework can load the typescript DO directly to HTML page. Existing the java object will be rewriting and transfer to typescript object. Exception Handling Existing business rules and validations will retain therefore error and warning message will remain the same. error/warning message are configured into database. I Connect framework manage it and fetch corresponding error/warning message based on error code. Angular6 will intercept related exception and redirect to exception page. File Uploading ECOM will support file uploading. If the file is accessible from client side, including local and remote file, ECOM will upload file to ECM. ECM will return document ID that will be captured in ECOM. Kenan LIC Existing OP launches Kenan KCC GUI to support billing and payment related transactions. In TO-BE solution, Kenan KCC is thick client application, ECOM is web-based application therefore LIC KCC GUI is not supported. User need to directly login KCC application to conduct the activity. NPP Client Existing NPP client generates service number, the business logic and validations are hardcoding in programs. In ECOM TO-BE solution, if service number generation factors are common and could be normalized as configurable parameters, the validation and service number format will be configurable. Code Table and Error Code Caching Code table and error code / message table will be stored in ECOM cache server. ECOM Front-end, iConnect Controller will read configuration data from cache sever. Besides code table and error code/message data, ECOM cache server stores frequently queried data in a temporary memory. It makes data easier to be accessed and reduces workloads for databases. Cache data will be persistent. Data will be there even if cache server stop or restart. Cache server will refresh itself every 24 hours. ECOM also provide near real-time cache refresh mechanism when configuration data is changed in database server. Order Management Related Info In Singtel BCC R2 release, ESOM will provide Service Order Management for non-Mobile products. ECOM integrate with ESOM for order fulfilment in ESOM. The Service Order, Work Order status and network related info changed in ESOM will be sync-up to ECOM via JMS ECOM will require work activity detail from ESOM via web service When order taker click button to check work order activity status, ECOM will call ESOM online API to retrieve activity detail and show it on screen DDI allocation and de-allocation will be performed by Number Management Team in ESOM moving forward. There two functions will be disabled in ECOM. Once the DDI information has been updated in ESOM, ESOM will be updating ECOM. Order taker is able to view the DDI info in ECOM. EET allocation will be in ESOM. It will be disabled in ECOM Update button on activity windows embedded on Service Order Screen will be disabled as the feature will be handled in ESOM Validations ECOM module will keep existing customer experience. Validations / business logic in Legacy front end will retain. ECOM is 3-tier architecture application. It will follow best practice to comply with InfoSec security policy. As and when SAVE and Submit etc. button is clicked to persist data in ECOM tables, selected business logic and security related validations will be duplicated in backend If pop-up screens and tabs associate these kinds of buttons that contains business validation rules, business validations would be duplicated in backend Browser Navigation Browser Back, Refresh button, F5 Key and right click will be disabled. Code to Config ECOM will provide “Code to Config” feature to make following common functions of network product actions become configurable: Table 6: Code to Config Supported Functions Function Name Issue Description setEnabled Enable or disable the target GUI field setMandatory Set the target GUI field to be mandatory or optional setSelectedItem Set the selected item of a combobox setDropdownList Set the list of items for a combobox setText Set the content of a text field. Can be a fixed text or from NPP or DB sequence createPortRef Save the current service number as a main port (DataPdtActivity.createPortRef) so that it can be used for PVC/EVC number generation cancelPortRef If the main port is cancelled, its status in OP_PVC_NO_TRACK needs to be updated to cancelled (DataPdtActivity.updatePortRefStatus) chkCondition Check that the condition is met. If not, an error message should be prompted chkFormat Check that the format of the target NPP aligns with the given Java regular expression. If validation fails, show error message chkRef Check that the target NPP is an existing ECOM service chkNumUniq Only applicable to the service number field. Check that the number does not conflict with any of the existing numbers of the same ext_id_ty in ECOM launchWin Launch another window based on the window name specified in the target_value setRcAnnotation For the NPP specified at TARGET_NAME, copy its value into the additional bill description of the RC. This is to facilitate showing NPP on the bill A new table OP_NW_PRDT_GUI_ACTION will be created to store actions (e.g. NPP updates/validations) to be performed when user interacts with the NPP window (e.g. clicks a button, changes a dropdown selection etc.) ECOM will provide UI for the table configuration. It would be accessible under Admin menu “Config Table Maintenance” screen. Mock-up screen is as below. title: R2 Billing KT.docx - Usage Rating
content: Usage Rating Create usage file as per the formats File to be placed at the path in Kenan Non-core server: /data/panda_int/ut01/ecom/inbound/raw_usage_ums Run the following Jobs from the path: /data/panda_app/ut01/ecom/scripts/jobs Kenan Non-Core $PWD/BIUMOV201D - to move file from Flemigo direc to other directory $PWD/BIIBND2C7D $PWD/BIUCHS201D - might fail with error code 255 due to checksum issues but moves file to director - /data/panda_var/ut01/ecom/input/BIUSPL201D $PWD/BIUSPL201D - checks sequence number ( if you got the error change the sequence number inside the file ) $PWD/BIUDIS201D $PWD/BIUBLV201D - Additional job for EDR NRC roaming usage-Might get errored with code 255 ( still proceed with next job) $PWD/BIUPPN201D/202D/203D/204D/ $PWD/BIUSBN201D/202D/203D... $PWD/BIUPCK201D Kenan core $PWD/BICOMG201D $PWD/BIMWAM201D - Might get errored with code 255 ( still proceed with next job) $PWD/BIPWAM301D Kenan Non Core $PWD/BIDUBC316D; collection processing $PWD/BIDUBC317D Note : Check the logs for error in case any of the job fails i.e.job exist code is not 0. IF all the jobs are successful verify the usage in DB as well as Kenan UI Query: Kenan Customer database Select * from CDR_DATA order by rate_dt desc; -- external_id in the table = service id Query: Kenan admin database for any rejections Select * from CDR_DATA_Work order by rate_dt desc; - select MIU_Error_code1 Go to table SYSTEM_MESSAGES Select * from SYSTEM_MESSAGES where message_number=’ MIU_Error_code1 Warm Usages: Usages Jobs for WBS Files: 1. File to be placed in Kenan NonCore Server: /data/panda_int/ut01/ecom/inbound/urms_wbs folder. 2. Run the following Jobs from the path: /data/panda_app/ut01/ecom/scripts/jobs Use warm usage flow to run WBS* files. 1. BIIBND2C8D -> Kenan NC 2. BIUCHS201R -> Kenan NC 3. BIUSPL201R -> Kenan NC 4. BIUPPW201R-> Kenan NC 5. BIUSBW201R-> Kenan NC 6. BICOMG201R > Kenan Core 7. BIMWAM201R-> Kenan Core 8. BIPWAM301R -> Kenan Core 9. BIDUBC301R -> Kenan NC Check the file in Usage_file_Status Table. If it’s in Status 10, The file processing is Completed. If we dont see any details in CDR_DATA or CDR_DATA_WORK, or File status. The whole usage file would be rejected and the rejected ones we can see in the path /app/FX/BP/data/usage/daily/error in Kenan Core. rev If LTP Is down (Meaning if last job of usage fails with error code) Run the below job in Kenan Core Server, BISLTP301O (biarbltp.ksh) - Job to Start LTP Process BITLTP301O (biarbstop.ksh) - Job to Stop LTP Process (Dont RUN THIS)

title: R2 Billing KT.docx - Proforma Bill
content: Proforma Bill DB Verifications/Patching before Proforma Query to get the arbor billing account number select a.ACCOUNT_NO from CUSTOMER_ID_ACCT_MAP a where a.EXTERNAL_ID in ('70974617') – external id is the billing account number from ECOM Query to check the billing cycle details. select ACCOUNT_NO,PREV_CUTOFF_DATE, PREV_BILL_DATE, NEXT_BILL_DATE, BILL_PERIOD, NO_BILL from CMF where ACCOUNT_NO =308038430; -- account_no is the account retrieved from query a Update bill cycle information based on the date for which you want data to be captured in the bill. Update MT_LAYER.CMF set PREV_CUTOFF_DATE = '07/11/22', next_bill_date='24/12/22',r PREV_BILL_DATE='24/11/22' where ACCOUNT_NO in ('308038824'); Next_bill_date- Bill_cycle.PPDD_date for the instance needs to be billed. Prev_bill_date – Bill_cycle.PPDD_date for the previous month instance . Prev_Cut_off_date – cutt off date from bil_cycle table Bill run can be done on any date after Prep date present in Bill_cycle table for that instance. Initiate proforma bill request from ECOM UI path: Billing and Payments ->Pro forma bill->request proforma Run the following jobs in sequence on Kenan servers Run cleanup job before doing proforma: $PWD/BIFSWP303D SNo. Job To be run in server Details of the Job 1 $PWD/BIPINT303D Kenan non core Creates entry in BI bill cycle queue 2 $PWD/BIBNOR371D Kenan core 3 $PWD/BIPERR303D Kenan non core 4 $PWD/BIFINT303D Kenan non core 5 $PWD/BIFNOR395D Kenan core 6 $PWD/BIFERR395D Kenan non core 7 $PWD/BIFLMS395D Kenan non core 8 $PWD/BIOBND303D Kenan non core Transfers the file to AMDD After running all jobs, need to run AMDD jobs from Jenkin –(point 6) Monitor Bill_Invoice table Check if account is billed successfully by running the below given query in Kenan customer DB SELECT * FROM bill_invoice WHERE account_no IN ('308038268'); Feed files are generated at the path: /data/panda_arc/ut01/ecom/interface/outbound/ Once all jobs are successful run AMDD jobs to check create the PDF from the path : /amdocs/apps/ams/amswrk1/var/bss/projs/dd/listener rj DD9LISTENERGE BYREQ - bfue_listener_ge.py rj DD9PRODGE BYREQ Cleanup script for AMDD: Script – bfue_clean_old_entries_sh After job is successful PDFs can be retrieved from ECOM from the path : Tools ->View Bills Or can be retrieved from ABP server path: /amdocs/apps/ams/amswrk1/var/bss/projs/dd/GEoutput/fi

title: R2 Billing KT.docx - End of Cycle Run
content: End of Cycle Run DB Verifications/Patching before EOC Query to get the arbor billing account number select a.ACCOUNT_NO from CUSTOMER_ID_ACCT_MAP a where a.EXTERNAL_ID in ('70974617') – external id is the billing account number from ECOM Query to check the billing cycle details. select ACCOUNT_NO,PREV_CUTOFF_DATE, PREV_BILL_DATE, NEXT_BILL_DATE, BILL_PERIOD, NO_BILL from CMF where ACCOUNT_NO ='308038820'; -- account_no is the account retrieved from query a Update bill cycle information based on the date for which you want data to be captured in the bill. Update MT_LAYER.CMF set PREV_CUTOFF_DATE = '07/11/22', next_bill_date='24/12/22', PREV_BILL_DATE='24/11/22' where ACCOUNT_NO in ('308038824'); Prev_bill_date – Bill_cycle table PPDD_date for that month Next_bill_date- next PPDD date from bill_cycle table Prev_Cut_off_date – cutt off date from bil_cycle table Note: Bill run can be done on any date after Prep date present in Bill_cycle table for that instance. Execute the following jobs in Sequence to perform EOC Path will be same for Kenan Non-Core and Core Servers: Integration: ECOM -> Kenan NC -> Kenan C -> Kenan NC -> AMDD -> ECOM Jobs will run on Server Date Jobs ---- Jobs run path: /data/panda_app/ut01/ecom/scripts/jobs Run clean-up job before doing BIP Production in Non-core server: $PWD/BIFSWP301D –will clean up old entries for the last instance being run. BIP --Kenan ############### If you have to run EOC multiple times in the same day. update bi_bill_day_distribution set BIPINIT_PROCESS_DT = NULL , indicator = 'N' where BIPINIT_PROCESS_DT = 'DATE on which bill run is executed' $PWD/BIPINT301D delete from bi_bill_cycle_queue where account_no not in (‘ ); update bi_bill_cycle_queue set ST = 1; - Run this after deleting other accounts. $PWD/BIPRPT301D $PWD/BIBNOR301D -- Kenan Core $PWD/BIPERR301D Payment --Kenan ############### $PWD/BIPUPT301D -- do not run this if running for backdated accounts. $PWD/BIPUBM301D -- payment jobs $PWD/BIPGLD301D BIF --Kenan ############### $PWD/BIFINT301D – After this job update ‘FT = 1’ in BI_BILL_CYCLE_QUEUE table if multiple accounts. $PWD/BIFNOR301D -- Kenan Core $PWD/BIFERR301D $PWD/BIFLMS301D $PWD/BIFSRT301D $PWD/BIOBND301D – transfer kenan feed file to AMDD(ABP) for PDF generation. $PWD/BIOBND360D - transfer kenan feed file to AMDD(ABP) for PDF generation. Note: To provide details to biz team AFP: AFP’s are present in the EOD directory in ABP output directory. Feed file: Search the feed file in directory in Kenan NC “/UAT-EBAT-KEN-NON-KBAT/data/disp/feed/ready/”. Feed file name can be referred from BILL_INVOICE.FILE_NAME for the BILL_REF_NO for our account. Bill Invoice detail: Refer below query Bill Invoice Detail extract query select b.description_text,a.* from bill_invoice_detail a , descriptions b where bill_ref_no in ('580347417','580347416','580347415','580347414','580347413','580347412','580347411') and a.description_code = b.description_code order by bill_ref_no; PDF: PDF from ABP output directory. UNTAR TAR file from EOC directory tar -xvzf .gz Check if account is billed successfully by running the below given query in Kenan customer DB SELECT * FROM bill_invoice WHERE account_no IN ('308038268'); Once all jobs are successful run AMDD jobs to check create the PDF from the path : /amdocs/apps/ams/amswrk1/var/bss/projs/dd/listener rj DD9LISTENERGE BYREQ rj DD9PRODGE BYREQ After job is successful PDFs can be retrieved from ECOM from the path : Tools ->View Bills Archive Job - Sent the PDF to ECOM Bill PDF can be taken from ABP DD path for GE i.e. amdocs/apps/ams/amswrk1/var/bss/projs/dd/GEoutput

title: R2 Billing KT.docx - REBIF Flow

Update BILL INVOICE TABLE FORMAT_STATUS = 0 FILE_NAME = NULL Update in case there are already entries in BBCQ table: Update BILL INVOICE SET FORMAT_STATUS = 0, FILE_NAME = NULL Where account_no in ( ) and Prep_staus=’1’ and bill_sequence_num= ; INSERT into BBCQ table if there are no entries to update. Update the PROC_SEQ_NO to the late sequence number, Account Number, BILL_REF_NO : Insert into bi_bill_cycle_queue (TYPE_INDICATOR,PROC_SEQ_NO,ACCOUNT_NO,CYCLE_FLAG,IN_USED,STATUS,LAST_UPDATE_ID,LAST_UPDATE_DT,BILL_REF_NO,BILL_REF_NO_RESETS,ST,FT,DISC_IN_USED,DISC_STATUS,BILL_FMT_OPT) values (1, 6690 , 308044359 ,'N',0,'BIFNOR301D','NCSKNC_APP',sysdate, 580359618 ,0,1,1,3333,'00000000',2); ADD STEPS for insert / update IN BBCQ After all the updates run the below jobs $PWD/BIFNOR301D -- Kenan Core – Validate BILL_INVOICE Table that FILE_NAME is updated with new file name. Once validated run below steps. $PWD/BIFERR301D $PWD/BIFLMS301D $PWD/BIFSRT301D $PWD/BIOBND301D $PWD/BIOBND360D Once the files are transferred to ABP run ABP jobs rj DD9LISTENERGE BYREQ rj DD9PRODGE BYREQ Note: Above steps are valid for EOC REBIF, for PROFORMA REBIF run the BIF flow from BIFNOR job as mentioned above.

title: R2 Billing KT.docx - VMB Flow
content: VMB Flow ECOM jobs to run to publish E-Bill customers to VMB FE - OPOP2W104D->OPOBND739D (FTP file to external system: EBILL_VMB) - account movement job Ebill registration from front end – run the following jobs in sequence OPIBND736D- pulls the files received from VMB and keeps it in location /data/panda_bat/ut01/ecom/input/ OPIW2P104D – delete all files , keep 1 file at a time OPIW2P104D – process the file – 1 file at a time OPOBND736D – file sent to VMB in format CORPPEGPTREQ*.dat VMB FE job is supposed to register the BRN in VMB FE and then (1) send the interface file to ECOM (to register as E-Bill for 2 BRNs) and (2) ECOM will send the list of accts registered as E-Bill belongs 2 BRNs back to VMB. To run the VMB process run below job in Kenan Non-core after bill run on the accounts is completed Kenan Non-Core BIBALC301D – this might end up with error code 255 ( which is okay) E-Bill - to generate E-bill run the following in sequence Kenan Non-Core BIILCA301D - - this should be success and should sent the file to location /data/VMB/ut01_corp/appln/ftp_bif AMDD bfue_vmb_erel_scp_ge.py - this is just for notification ( not mandatory to run) To notify user after EBill generation run bfue_extract_vmb_email.py To view bill on VMB following jobs need to be run on Kenan Non-core Bif Should be present at the path : /data/VMB/ut01_corp/appln/ftp_bif file should be in Ifbifiv*.dat.gz format Path: /app/VMB/ut01_corp/appln/scripts ./cfset.sh ./uzbif.sh ./pegasus_m.sh ./pegasus_u.sh ./createpath.sh ./extsvc.sh ./split_u.sh ./extract.sh ./split_m.sh ./split_s.sh ./recon_u_01.sh ./recon_u_02.sh ./recon_u_03.sh ./zpbif.sh Once jobs are run verify accounts at the path: /app/VMB/ut01_corp/appln/ebill/output/temp_account – unzip the file and verify the accounts. /data/VMB/ut01_corp/appl/ebill/data/2023/ UDF VMB – Support Jobs Input Dat file expected with below namining convention at AMDD server TRANUDFZIPREQ20211201101113.dat -> VBZIPREQ20220602.dat -> VMB adhoc Files will be received from UDF at the path : /amdocs/apps/ams/amswrk1/var/bss/projs/bl/interfaces/input Run AR3GWLSTR job to transfer input file in required path. /amdocs/apps/ams/amswrk1/var/bss/projs/bl/VMB Run “bfue_fetch_brn_adhoc_data.py” to generate PDF and transfer and send notification to AMDD. Verify output at path : /amdocs/apps/ams/amswrk1/var/bss/projs/dd/GEoutput/VMB/Adhoc/10/13 For recurring files run bfue_fetch_brn_recur_data.py from path /amdocs/apps/ams/amswrk1/pbin/app/AMDD_VMB

content: GL flow Tables : Jnl_runs_status , jnl_detail , jnl_trans , bi_Journal_storage Weekly Jobs that need to be run KNC: Kenan Non core KC: Kenan Core BIJINT301W – KNC Functions: Updates Jnl_runs.jnl_run_dt of jnl_type 1,and , 3 to system dates to before BIJMAN301/401/501/601M triggers Arbor main journal cycle. Input: Jnl_runs_status – the last journal run must be a successful run Output: Jnl_runs Update the path and process for BIJERA301W BIJMAN301W – KC – In case of missing keys issue run job BIJERA301W in Kenan Non Core. Follow below steps: Once BIJMAN301W fails with JNL KEYS error in logs Path for BIJERA in Kenan Non-Core: “/data/panda_bat/ut01/ecom/input/BIJERA301W” Process the file from the jobs path by running job BIJERA301W . Once BIJERA301W is completed update JNL_KEYS .ACTIVE_DATE to any older date for the newly inserted records where JNL_CODE_ID is 666666666. Generally change the year from current to a year or 2 back for e.g: if year is 2023 change it to 2021 or 2022. Functions: Type1: Journal billed charges Type2: Journal unbilled charges Type3: Journal payments/payment rev/deposits/refunds charges Transactions before jnl_end_dt will be picked by run Journal runs in sequence from type 1 and 3 for weekly run. Output: Jnl_trans Jnl_detail Jnl_runs_status – to check if runs_status =1(success) BIJFCO301W – KNC Functions: Converts payment/payment reversal/refund transactions with invoice currency different from the G/L currency (i.e., base currency e.g., SGD) Computes foreign exchange gain/loss arises from the floating exchange rate. Input: Jnl_Detail table Output: Bi_Hq_FX_Jnl_detail; Bi_sgo_Jnl_detail Troubles shooting: Activity log. BIJFUP301W - KNC BIJSGP301W - KNC BIJSGU301W - KNC BIJINT302W – KNC Functions: Update jnl_runs.jnl_run_dt of jnl_type 4 to system date to enable Arbor journal run . Input: Jnl_runs_status Jnl_runs Output: Jnl_runs Troubles shooting: Job log. BIJMAN302W - KC - Feed file path : /UAT-EBAT-KEN-NON-KBAT/data/jnl/ready ( can do till here also to start next week) Functions: Generate Arbor journal feed file Input: Jnl_trans Output: Arbor journal feed file Jnl_runs_status Troubles shooting: Activity log –error not common. Common error: No schedule run, jnl_runs.jnl_end_dt not updated, checked if BIJINT*02M was successful KNC Path - /data/panda_bat/ut01/ecom/data/jnl/ready àplace the feed file here BIJPRE301W – KNC Functions: Extract data from BI_SGO_JNL_DETAIL and insert into BI_JNL_TEMP. Input: BI_SGO_JNL_DETAIL Output: BI_JNL_TEMP BIJGRC301W – KNC Functions: To cater for multiple GRC customers in BI_MASTER_KEYS, obtain account’s information from CMF and BILL_INVOICE, based on this to compute amount from BILL_INVOICE_DISCOUNT, if no records in BILL_INVOICE_DISCOUNT, then obtain amount from BILL_INVOICE_DETAIL,then updated the data in to BI_JNL_CHG_TXNS table Input: BI_MASTER_KEYS CMF BILL_INVOICE BILL_INVOICE_DISCOUNT BILL_INVOICE_DETAIL Output: BI_JNL_CHG_TXNS (admin table) BI_FILE_HIST BIJRTG301W – KNC Functions: To interpret the type of markup/re-rating, and to obtain the re-rated amount for the respective PIC. All the value is to be populated into BI_JNL_MARKUP_RERATE table Input: CMF BILL_INVOICE BILL_INVOICE_DETAIL Bill_equip_detail Output: BI_JNL_MARKUP_RERATE (admin table) BI_JNL_REJECTS BI_FILE_HIST BIJPRO301W - KNC - create entries in BJS Functions: Process Arbor journal feed file from type 4 run and generate the appropriate accounting debit and credit entries Insert records into bi_journal_storage In this process, split revenue for billed OBR . Input: Arbor journal feed files: input directory /${HOSTNAME}/${PRJ_ENV}/pegasus/data/jnl/ready/ BI_JNL_MARKUP_RERATE(For outbound roaming) Output: Bi_journal_storage BI_JNL_REJECTS Troubles shooting: Activity log and control report. Common errors: No files input directory /${HOSTNAME}/${PRJ_ENV}/pegasus/data/jnl/ready Input directory in INI file incorrect The same file is processed more than once, to process the files again, delete record from bi_file_hist table where module_id=’bij_jn_p_c1/2/3/4/’ [Note: jnl_ref_no &server_id found in header of file; unique identifier of a file in BI_file_hist] IN case of failure of this JOB For cleanup if BIJPRO(m) fails, move the files from “/data/ panda_var /ut01/ecom/data/jnl/ready” Insert the same files again in KNC path “/data/ panda_bat /ut01/ecom/data/jnl/ready” BIJBJS201W – KNC Functions: Move data of BI_JOURNAL_STORAGE from 4 custom servers into admin server. Input: bi_journal_storage (4 custom servers) Output: Bi_journal_storage(admin server) Fetch GL reports from path: “/data/panda_bat/ut01/ecom/actuate_rpts” gl_account_bk = '23' is for SGO GERMANY Monthly Jobs that need to be run: BIJINT301M - KNC BIJMAN301M – KC - In case of missing keys issue run job BIJERA301M in Kenan NC IF BIJMAN fails run BIJERA301M job in Kenan NON Core server. title: R2 Billing KT.docx - Collection Jobs
content: Collection Jobs Two Flows – Force collection and Automatic collection Force collection the account from CRM Run Force Collection extract process from MCO. Then check the csv file on /app/FX/BP/custom_jobs/SingtelKenanDataProcessor/data/ready in Kenan Core server Run the script – LoadForceCollectionAccounts.sh from the path /app/FX/BP/custom_jobs/SingtelKenanDataProcessor Run the script - ExtractCollectionCandidates.sh app/FX/BP/custom_jobs/SDP Verify file created at- /app/FX/BP/data/collections/data/done Once the file is in done directory run below job to move the file to ABP in Kenan Non-Core BICCMV301D BIOBND705D And file is SFTP to ABP- /amdocs/apps/ams/amswrk1/var/bss/projs/cl/interfaces/input/GATEKEEPER Run the following jobs in ABP server and check file entry is created in AC1_control table Query: select * from ac1_control where file_name like ‘%Collection%’ order by sys_creation_date desc; 1. rj AR3GWLSTR BYREQ 2. rj CL9GATEKEEPER BYREQ 3. rj CL9EVALUATOR BYREQ Account will be moved to collection in Cl1_coll_entity table in ABP Query: select * from cl1_coll_entity where entity_id= order by sys_creation_date desc; Transaction to be updated from CL (ABP) to ECOM to update the collection status. ECOM should show customer is in collection. To set the credit rating and blacklist indicator in ECOM and CRM CL9CRDRTBLCLC -->> FA Level CM9BLCKUPDCRM_01_1 --->> Contact Level – these have to be run in AMC ( check if can configure in Jenkins) Collection letter jobs (can be run from AMC) CCS1RPJD BYREQ/ENDDAY - Change from Pending to Extracted in CCS1_request table in ABP rj CCS1BGB BYREQ – this will change the status to processed in CCS1_request table Rj ADD3AREXTR BYREQ - this will create entry in ADD3_LETTER_REQUEST Table Rj ADD3LMSEOD BYREQ-this will create entry in AD3_LETTER_ARCHIVE Table The Pdf Path should be à /amdocs/apps/ams/amswrk1/var/bss/projs/dd/letters/ Retrial steps: 1. Bring CCS1RPJD daemon down 2. Run following commands for request to reprocess in ccs1_request table update ccs1_request set status_Code='PENDING' where request_id=’Request_id’; delete from CCS1_REQ_XTRCT_CTRL where request_id=’Request_id’; delete from CCS1_REQ_DATA_SGMT where request_id=’Request_id’; delete from CCS1_REQ_ACTIVITY where request_id=’Request_id’; 3. Bring CCS1RPJD daemon up 4. Check in CCS1_REQUEST table if status_code changed to ‘EXTRACTED’ 5. Run pu job 6. Check in CCS1_REQUEST table if status_code changed to ‘PROCESSED’ For Write off accounts Run rj CL9WOEXT BYREQ in ABP If any entry in CL9_APPROVED_WRT_OFF with STATUS 'E' and SYS_UPDATE_DATE as current date, then update status back to 'P' & rerun the job Automatic collection Steps Run the script - ExtractCollectionCandidates.sh /app/FX/BP/custom_jobs/SDP from kenan core server. Verify file created at- /app/FX/BP/data/collections/data/done Once the file is in done directory run below job to move the file to ABP in Kenan Non-Core Run the following Jobs from the path: /data/panda_app/ut01/ecom/scripts/jobs BICCMV301D ( this needs to be run via Kenan Non Core server ) BIOBND705D And file is SFTP to ABP- /amdocs/apps/ams/amswrk1/var/bss/projs/cl/interfaces/input/GATEKEEPER Run the following jobs in ABP server and check file entry is created in AC1_control table Query: select * from ac1_control where file_name like ‘%Collection%’ order by sys_creation_date desc; 1. rj AR3GWLSTR BYREQ 2. rj CL9GATEKEEPER BYREQ 3. rj CL9EVALUATOR BYREQ Account will be moved to collection in Cl1_coll_entity table in ABP Query: select * from cl1_coll_entity where entity_id= order by sys_creation_date desc; Reminder Fee Jobs Run rj CL9REMFEEEXT BYREQ in ABP File will be generated at path /amdocs/apps/ams/amswrk1/var/bass/projs/cl/interfaces/output/R2REMEXTREQ folder Run rj AR3GWLSTR BYREQ – file should be moved to kenan Collections (via TRB) --> ECOM ( OPOFEE101D ) --> Kenan Kenan jobs are posting are BICFEE201D , BICNRC301D ================================================================ Debit transfer job: BIBDBT301D- Kenan core File will be generated at /data/panda_bat/ut01/ecom/actuate_rpts ================================================ File is placed in data/panda_app/st01/arst/ODARLRB/LRB_US - Revised bill

The job ODARLPDF3D will read the new file name and upload the files to ECM after removing the prefix New outbound job ODAROBND3D will be created to sftp files to datapost copied by ODARPDF3D to Datapost server. New recon job ODARRECOND will be created to create the recon report for the files successfully transferred to DataPost. Job ODARMAIL4D - send “DP upload recon report” to datapost user list ManageDocumentService.uploadDocument API to upload document to ECM. If the bill image is uploaded successfully, it will insert record into OP_REVISED_BILL_UPLOAD table. $PWD/ODARCKNA1D $PWD/ODARGIND2D $PWD/ODARLPDF3D J obs to push config from ECOM to NGOST , OFDUMP102D->OFOBND101D

title: Singtel Spring R2 ESOM High Level Design v2.16.docx - Solution Overview
content: Solution Overview Accenture ESOM (Enterprise Service Order Management) solution approach is to re-platform legacy Pegasus OM onto a more robust and modern TIBCO Orchestration Suite. TIBCO is a proven service-oriented architecture, messaging and event processing technology. The basis of the strategy to re-platform the existing solution onto TIBCO platform are Existing functionalities have already been proven working in current Singtel ecosystems Vitria components (e.g. channel, automator) can be mapped to TIBCO BusinessWorks and BusinessEvents components (e.g. listener, workflow). Below illustrate the legacy applications that will be uplifted into ESOM application. Figure 1: Legacy Application Uplifted onto ESOM Application ESOM Application Description ESOM Web Portal ESOM OM Web Portal is a graphical user interface that acts as the front-end interface for users to perform order fulfilment activities. It is designed to re-platform the existing Order Management functionalities in legacy OPOM such as OM Inbox and Work Order Details. COM Order Broker COM Order Broker is a new component introduced in the ESOM stack of application. Its primary role is to support the integration with ECOM to receive request form ECOM and sending key status notification back. COM Order Broker will be implemented on TIBCO BusinessWorks. OM Workflow Engine Legacy OM related Vitria Projects will be uplifted onto OM Workflow Engine. Leveraging on the workflow engine and integration capability of TIBCO BusinessWorks as well as the event processing capability of TIBCO BusinessEvents, Vitria components can be ported over to the new TIBCO platform. OM Service Layer OM Service Layer houses all the legacy EJBs and Java application which are residing in BES onto the JBoss EAP Server. OM Batch Legacy OM Batch will be uplifted onto Spring Batch framework. Below diagram illustrates the high-level solution blueprint of ESOM and the next few chapters will be discussing about the functional, application, technical overview of the ESOM solution. Figure 2: ESOM Solution Blueprint Chapter Solution Stack 3 ESOM Data Model 4 ECOM and ESOM Integration 5 ESOM and ESM Integration 6 COM Order Broker 7 OM Workflow Engine 8 OM Service Layer 9 Batch Architecture 10 ESOM Web Portal

title: Singtel Spring R2 ESOM High Level Design v2.16.docx - Application Architecture
content: Application Architecture Figure 3: ESOM Application Architecture ESOM Application Description ESOM Web Portal ESOM OM Web Portal will be deployed on JBoss EAP and will be consuming internal services from OM Service Layer to invoke any backend EJBs. COM Order Broker COM Order Broker is implemented using TIBCO Business Work and will be deployed on TIBCO Server. COM Order Broker will be connecting to the JMS queue on ECOM EIL system and consuming the request messages. OM Workflow Engine OM Workflow Engine is implemented using TIBCO Business Work and TIBCO BusinessEvents and will be deployed on TIBCO Server. OM Workflow Engine leverages on TIBCO EMS for internal transport layer. OM Workflow Engine exposes services for ECOM and ESM to consume as well. OM Service Layer OM Service Layer houses all the legacy EJBs and will be deployed on JBoss EAP. EJBs will be wrapped around with internal webservices consumed by ESOM Web Portal, OM Workflow Engine and OM Batch. OM Service Layer exposes services for ESM to consume as well. OM Batch Legacy OM Batch will be uplifted onto Spring Batch framework deployed on ESOM server. OM Batch leverage on Singtel Control-M as the Job Scheduler. OM Batch will consume services from OM Service Layer to invoke the backend EJBs. ESOM Database ESOM Database will be implemented using Oracle Database 19c.

title: Singtel Spring R2 ESOM High Level Design v2.16.docx - Functional Overview
content: Functional Overview ESOM is an uplift of legacy OM to support the fulfilment and service provisioning of Enterprise and SME products. In general, ESOM takes in request (Order and Non-order requests) from the Northbound ordering application (i.e. ECOM) and performs order decomposition and orchestration of provisioning steps. It will also integrate with the Southbound network activation system or other external system for work order details download. Figure 4: ESOM Northbound and Southbound Interaction ESOM supports the same GE and SME products configured in legacy OPOM except for Enterprise Mobile. It is expected for ECOM to send down Enterprise Mobile related orders to NetCracker (NC) SOM for service provisioning. Figure 5: Order flow to NCSOM and ESOM

title: Singtel Spring R2 ESOM High Level Design v2.16.docx - ESOM Ordering Request Functional Flow
content: ESOM Ordering Request Functional Flow Below describes the high-level functional flow for ESOM ordering request from the point ECOM sends down the order request till order closure. Figure 6: ESOM Functional Flow Process Description Illustration Order Receipt and Order Validation COM Order Broker receives order request from ECOM JMS queue and starts the validation process 2 levels for validation will be performed by COM Order Broker and any Service/Work orders that failed validation will be rejected back to ECOM Once validation has passed, this is when the Service Order and Work Order will be persisted into ESOM database for the first time. Pre-Processing and Decomposition ESOM Workflow Engine will then pick up the Work Order record and the Work Order will go through order decomposition. OM Markers will be generated out as part of the order decomposition. Order Orchestration Once OM Markers are generated, activities will be derived based on the OM Markers to Activities configuration mapping. ESOM Workflow Engine will then orchestrate through the fulfilment activities. Order Completion Once all the fulfilment activities are completed, ESOM Workflow Engine will then mark the work order as completed. Order Closure Order Closure Batch Job will then be kicked in to pick up all completed work orders for closure. The Order Closure Batch will instantiate the service tied to the work order and update the ESOM service tables.

title: Singtel Spring R2 ESOM High Level Design v2.16.docx - ESOM Data Model
content: ESOM Data Model This section discusses on the ESOM data model and the various entities that make up the data model. ESOM will be retaining the data model from legacy OPOM to support the fulfilment and provisioning processes. In general, ESOM data model can be classified into 5 categories: ESOM User Profile defines the user access management within ESOM Web Portal and the privileges assigned to the various user groups Service Order and Work Order are transactional requests submitted into ESOM from ECOM for order fulfilment and provisioning. They contain the relevant network product transactions and fulfilment instructions required to provision the service. Upon successful provisioning of the service, a Service Profile will be instantiated in ESOM. The service profile will be necessary for future modification or cessation of the service upon any Service Order and Work Order requests from ECOM. Product Configuration defines the product data model used to represent the offerings from Singtel to support fulfilment purposes. Fulfilment Rules are a set of decomposition and fulfilment configuration required to support service provisioning. Figure 8: ESOM Data Model

title: Singtel Spring R2 ESOM High Level Design v2.16.docx - ESOM User Profile
content: ESOM User Profile ESOM will be uplifting the same User to User Role and Screen Function mapping concept from Pegasus SSO. The role will in turn determine which OM Role a user will be assigned to. User Role and Function Mapping controls which ESOM screens you will be authorized to access while OM Roles determine what access level you will be entitled after gaining access to a screen. Figure 9: ESOM User Profile Overview User Profile Entity Description ESOM User Describes the user definition of ESOM Web Portal. User Role Describes the user role that is assigned to the user. Each user can have one or more than one role mapping. Screen Function Describes the screens access that a User or Role is assigned to. Each Role can have more than one and minimum one screen mapping. OM Role Describes the OM Role a user is assigned to. OM Roles comprises Supervisor Performer Controller Viewer Contractor Security Group Security Group can be mapped to a user to determine the security access a user has on an ESOM screen (eg. Access to click on a specific button) or certain restriction to be removed from a user (eg. Disabling of a button). OM Group Describes the OM Group in which the user is assigned to. Each user can have more than one OM Group assigned.

title: Singtel Spring R2 ESOM High Level Design v2.16.docx - Customer Account
content: Customer Account Only minimal Customer Account related information are mastered in ESOM Service Profile. This information is required in ESOM for provisioning purpose and/or to be downloaded to ESOM integrating system. Below table list down the Customer Account related entities that will be mastered. S/N Entity Description 1 Customer Name Name of the Customer subscribing to the service 2 Account ID Internal Customer Account ID 3 Customer ID External Customer Account ID 4 Customer ID Type Customer ID Type (Eg. “Unique Entity Number (UEN)”, “National Registration Identity Card (NRIC)”, etc. 5 Customer Classification Customer Classification (eg. “BizSales (Platinum)”, “Carrier Services”, etc. 6 Owning Entity Customer owning entity (eg. “Singapore”,” UK”, etc.) 7 VIP Code VIP Code (eg. “Government”, “Public Service Organisation”, etc.) 8 Secret Account Indicator Indicator whether Customer Account is treated as a secret account 9 Sensitive Indicator Indicator whether Customer Account is a sensitive account Sensitive Customer Account In ESOM, the sensitive customer account will continue be stored and maintained in OP_SENSITIVE_CUST_ACCT. Customer accounts who are classified as a sensitive account will have their view access limited to certain OM Users. In ESOM Web Portal, only OM Users who have the right access to view sensitive customer accounts can search for their related order details and view their service instance profiles. OM Users without the access will not be able to view any order details or service instance profiles that are tied to a sensitive customer account. OM Admin Users will be able to use the Admin Screens in ESOM Web Portal to create and modify existing sensitive customer accounts records. Figure 19: Access to Sensitive Customer Account Entity Relationship Below illustrates the entity relationship based on the database tables. Figure 20: Customer Account Entity Relationship

title: Singtel Spring R2 ESOM High Level Design v2.16.docx - Service Instance
content: Service Instance Service Instance in ESOM represents the provisioning profile a customer has subscribed to and it contains the following: Service Address (If applicable to the service) Network Product Instance Network Product Parameter Instance Product Tie Below table list down the Service Instance related entities that will be mastered. S/N Entity Description 1 Service Instance ID System Service Instance ID 2 Billing Account ID Billing Account ID service is tied to 3 Service Type Service Type (eg. TS) 4 Arbor Service Type Arbor Service Type (eg. 401) 5 Rental Tariff Group Rental Tariff Group 6 XDirectory Indicator XDirectory Indicator 7 Service Instance Status Current status of the service instance 8 Start Date Start date of the service 9 End Date End date of the service Service Instance State Model Below illustrates the state model of the Service Instance status in ESOM. Figure 23: ESOM Service Instance State Model S/N Status Description 1 New Status of the Service Instance when it is first persisted into the database. Service is yet to be active as the corresponding Provide Work Order has not been fulfilled successfully. 2 Active Service has been successfully instantiated and service is active now. 3 Ceased Service has been ceased upon request from ECOM. 4 Cancelled Service Instance has been cancelled upon request from ECOM before Provide Work Order has been fulfilled successfully. 5 Bar Premium VAS TD0 Service has undergone a temporary disconnect (Barring of premium VAS) due to collection scenario. This status is only applicable for the following Arbor Service Type. TS – DEL TS – MoIP 6 2-Way TD/ Total TD Service has undergone a total temporary disconnect due to collection scenario. This status is only applicable for the following Arbor Service Type. IPTV SingNet (Only applicable to “Non-Corp” SingNet Products) SaaS (Excluding NEOfficeNoFrills products) TS – PABX TS – PhoneNet TS – Vcall VS – Virtual Services Service Instance under TOS Note that a service instance can be TOS (Temporary out of Service) but TOS is not a valid service instance status from a system perspective. Just like legacy OPOM, a TOS service instance will have its service instance status remain as “Active” but an active TOS Network Product instance will exist under the service instance. Figure 24: A Service Instance that is TOS TOS Service Instance is only applicable to specific Product Type (Service Type). Below is the list of valid TOS Network Product Code configured. S/N TOS Network Product Code Network Product Description 1 DEL0056 Temporary Out of Service 2 ISD0035 Temporary Out Of Service For ISDN 2 3 ISD0036 Temporary Out Of Service For ISDN 30 4 MOP0056 MoIP Temporary Out of Service 5 SGN0021 TOS due to customer request Network Product Instance and NPP Every Service Instance in ESOM will have a Mainline Network Product Instance and zero-to-many VAS Network Product Instance beneath it. Network Product serves as the technical product of a service and captures the necessary attributes (a.k.a Network Product Parameters) required for provisioning. Network Product Instance and its corresponding NPP are instantiated upon work order closure. Figure 25: Network Product Instance and NPPs under Service Instance Below table list down the key Network Product Instance related entities that will be mastered. S/N Entity Description 1 Network Product Instance ID System Network Product Instance ID 2 Network Product Code System Identifier for the Network Product Instance 3 Status Status of the Network Product Instance 4 Start Date Start Date of the Network Product Instance 5 End Date End Date of the Network Product Instance 6 Line No Line No of the Network Product Instance. Only applicable for multi-lines products such as PABX Aux Line, ISDN Aux Lines, etc. Below table list down the key Network Product Parameters related entities that will be mastered. S/N Entity Description 1 Network Product Parameter Name Descriptive name of the Network Product Parameter 2 Network Product Parameter Value Value of the Network Product Parameter Network Product Instance State Model Below illustrates the state model of the Network Product Instance status in ESOM. Figure 26: Network Product Instance Status State Model S/N Status Description 1 Active Indicates that the current Network Product Instance is active 2 Inactive Indicates that the current Network Product Instance is inactive Service Instance Tie ESOM will be uplifting the same Service Instance Tie concept from legacy OPOM. Service Instance Tie is a logical grouping of two or more services together with no hierarchy relationship (i.e Parent or Child). Service Instance Ties are created in ECOM and passed down to ESOM as part of the Work Order payload. ESOM will be instantiating the Service Instance Tie details upon Work Order closure. Service Instance Tie comprises of 3 different tie types: Circuit Tie does a logical grouping of service instances based on related products ED/PD Tie does a logical grouping of service instances with Exchange Diversity (ED) and Path Diversity (PD) relationship. This is applicable to specific products Port Tie does a logical grouping of services instances based on related products leveraging on the same network and infrastructure. Figure 27: ESOM Service Instance Tie Below illustrates an example of a circuit tie that ties two service instances together. Figure 28: A Service Tie (Circuit Tie Type) grouping 2 service instances together Below table list down the key Service Tie related entities that will be mastered. S/N Entity Description 1 Service Tie ID System Service Tie Instance ID 2 Service Tie Type Service Tie Type 3 Service Tie Description Service Tie Description 4 Start Date Start Date of the Service Tie 5 End Date End Date of the Service Tie 6 Cancel Reason Cancellation Reason of the Service Tie Service Instance Entity Relationship Below illustrates the entity relationship of Service Instance based on the database tables. Figure 29: Entity Relationship of Service Profile

title: Singtel Spring R2 ESOM High Level Design v2.16.docx - Network Model
content: Network Model Network Product Network Products are provisioning entities containing various provisioning attributes to be passed down to the network teams or activation systems for fulfilment purposes. Figure 32: Illustration of the ESOM Network Product Model The above illustrates the basic Network Product model within ESOM. Network Products can be primarily categorized into various levels, indicating if they are mainline or VASes. Each service in ESOM contains a set of Network Products, and it must have one and only one mainline Network Product, while Network Products of other levels can be included multiple times. Figure 33: Illustration of ESOM Product Model for ISDN For specific multi-line products, such as ISDN, PABX, i-Phonenet (BizVoice) and Phonenet, further elements of the ESOM product model are needed to model them accordingly. Apart from mainline and VASes, other various levels of Network Products are required (e.g. Auxiliary Lines and DDI Lines) to model the additional lines modelled under the same product mainline. For the additional lines, each instance is tied to a Line Number, which is used to identify the specific instance of each additional line, and its sequence in the service and / or order. Each line can then have VASes and DDI lines captured under them. Furthermore, not all Network Products are tied to billing components. In such instances, they are modelled as “Pure Network Products”, and are expected to be added manually on top of the existing Network Products associated to billing components during the process of order capture. As the Network Product entity is a shared concept between ESOM and its upstream enterprise order capture system, any Network Product configurations required for ESOM should also be configured within the upstream enterprise order capture system. Such configurations for both systems are expected to be aligned operationally. Entity Name Entity Description Network Product Code Unique identifier of the configured Network Product Level Indicator Identifies the level of the Network Product Level Indicator Level Indicator Description 1 Mainline 2 Auxiliary Line 3 VAS 4 Slave 5 DDI 6 DID 7 EE Each Service order and work order must have one and only one mainline Network Product Product Type Identifies the type of Network Product Product Type Product Type Description 0 Neither Indicates that this Network Product is mapped to a billing component and can be used in any order type 1 Change Indicates that this Network Product is mapped to a billing component and can only be used in a Change work order type 2 Pure Network Product Indicates that this Network Product is not mapped to any billing component but can be used in any order type. Service Type Service Type that has been configured to the Network Product Unique Indicator Indicates if the Network Product is unique. If “Y”, there can only be one active instance of this Network Product per Service instance. Required Parameter Indicator Indicates if there are mandatory Network Product Parameters to be populated during order capture / provisioning. Network Product Long Description Detailed description of the Network Product Network Product Description Brief description of the Network Product Status Indicates the status of the Network Product configuration. Active Network Products are valid Network Products in ESOM that will trigger provisioning flows. Status Status Description 1 Active 2 Inactive Object Name Defines what is the screen name that shall be launched when the NPP button is being selected during order fulfilment. Service Group Defines the service group configured to the Network Product. Service groups are used to associate Network Products of similar ordering / provisioning behaviors together. (e.g. Service Number format). Figure 34: Network Product Definition Table (OP_NW_PRDT_CD) The figure above shows the table structure and details captured in the Network Product configuration and definition table. All Network Products that are supported in ESOM are captured and defined within this table. Network Product Parameters Figure 35: Illustration of the relationship between Network Product and NPPs Network Product Parameters (NPPs) are provisioning attributes stored and associated to a Network Product. They are entities holding information that are required by downstream network systems and / or fulfilment teams during the provisioning process. They can be associated to any levels of Network Product. NPPs are optional entities belonging to a Network Product, with each Network Product having the possibility of containing numerous NPPs. Entity Name Entity Description Parameter Name Name of the NPP Network Product Code Network Product code of the NPP that has been defined against Parameter Type Identifies the type of NPP Parameter Type Parameter Type Description External ID Parameter is identified as an external ID that can be used to identify an instance of the service Network Product Parameter The standard configuration for NPPs, where they will be assetized in ESOM as part of the service image upon order closure. Network Product Parameter (Transactional) A set of transaction NPPs that will only be visible during the lifetime of the order. Upon order closure, such NPPs would not be assetized as part of the service image within ESOM. Parameter Description Detailed description of the NPP Status Indicates the status of the NPP configuration. Status Status Description 1 Active 2 Inactive External ID Type Identifies the type of External ID will be stored in ESOM Figure 36: NPP Definition Table (OP_NW_PRDT_PARA_CD) The figure above shows the table structure of how NPPs are being configured in ESOM. Each NPP configured shall be inserted as an entry into the NPP definition table. Network Product Parameter GUI Definitions Figure 37: Screengrab of ESOM NPP Screen ESOM adopts a configurations-driven NPP rendering approach, as supported in legacy OPOM. Referencing the figure above, each NPP and button defined in the screengrab are lines of configurations captured within the GUI definition table. These NPPs may be entered / modified by users of the upstream order capture system, or by the provisioning team / system during the order fulfilment process in ESOM. Each NPP is governed by a set of GUI rules configured within ESOM that determines if their behaviour during the various stages of provisioning. Entity Name Entity Description Action Code Defines the eligibility of this GUI item behaviour based on the Network Product action (if the Network Product is added / modified / ceased during the order) Action Code Action Code Description 1 Provide 2 Change 3 Cease Parameter Name Name of the parameter Network Product Code Network Product code of the parameter that has been defined against Sequence Number Defines the order that the parameter is displayed on the screen. Control Type Determines the type of parameters Button: Clickable window button Combo: Dropdown menu PAN: Alphanumeric text field PDC: Numeric decimal field PDT: Date field PNO: Numeric text field stored as text PNU: Numeric text field stored as number Control Label Defines the display value of the parameter Read Only Indicator Determines the access control of the parameter Read Only Indicator Read Only Indicator Description 0 Control is disabled, with data saved into the database. 2 Control is enabled, with data saved into the database. 3 4 Control is disabled, with data not saved into the database. Users would not be able to change the value. 6 Control is enabled, with data not saved into the database. 7 8 Control is hidden, with data saved into the database. 9 Control is hidden, with data not saved into the database. Control Parameter Defines the enhanced behaviour of the control, dependent on the control type. Control Type Description Examples Button Shortcut key b DButton Combo Dropdown List identifier ( in TA_MASTER_CD) PORT_INTF PAN Identifier the formatting rules of this field. ( default value, maximum length of field, masked value) %,11,1900 PDC PDT PNO PNU Mandatory Indicator Determines if the NPP is mandatory Mandatory Indicator Mandatory Indicator Description 0 Control is not mandatory. 2 Control is mandatory 3 Status Indicates the status of the GUI configuration Status Status Description 1 Active 2 Inactive Figure 38: GUI Definition Table (OP_NW_PRDT_GUI_DEF) The table above captures the GUI definitions configured. Each Network Product that has NPPs will have a set of GUI controls configured against them. These GUI controls are triggered when the NPP details of a Network Product are selected for display or modification. Each control’s behaviour is governed by the Network Product action of the associated Network Product. (e.g. When a Network Product is being added to an order, the controls for Network Product Action “Provide” are triggered). The configured controls are then interpreted to enhance the control behaviour on the GUI.

title: Singtel Spring R2 ESOM High Level Design v2.16.docx - OM Markers
content: OM Markers Order Management (OM) Markers are the building blocks of provisioning flows and are derived after order decomposition. They serve as a logical set of activities grouped together to promote reusability. Entity Name Entity Description OM Marker Unique identifier of the OM Marker Marker Description Description of the OM Marker Service Type Defines the service type that is associated to this OM marker Status Indicates the status of the OM Marker configuration. Status Status Description 1 Active 2 Inactive Figure 39: OM Marker Definition Table (OP_OM_MARKER_MAST) The table above captures the configurations detailed within the OM Marker definitions table. Each OM Marker would first have to be configured within this table. Subsequently, triggers for the OM Markers can then be mapped via 3 conditions, namely Association to Network Product and NPPs Association to order conditions Association to an existing service / instanced image. OM Markers to Network Products and NPP Figure 40: Illustration of the relationship between Network Product / NPP with OM Markers In the illustration above, OM Marker “NCP1PL” is mapped to Network Product “CNP0001”, while OM Marker “NREGPT” is mapped to NPP “Port Speed”. This example illustrates the flexibility of OM Markers being mapped to both Network Products and NPP. Entity Name Entity Description OM Marker Unique identifier of the OM Marker Network Product Code Indicates the Network Product that the defined OM Marker is associated to Parameter Name Indicates the NPP that is mapped to the condition required to generate the defined OM Marker When the value is null, it indicates the OM Marker will be generated regardless of conditions. Parameter Value Indicates the value of the NPP that is mapped to the condition required to generate the defined OM Marker When the value is null, it indicates that the OM Marker will be generated for all values of a given NPP. Status Indicates the status of the OM Marker to Network Product / NPP mapping. Status Status Description 1 Active 2 Inactive Network Product Action Indicates under which condition of the Network Product will the OM Marker be generated. Network Product Action Network Product Action Description All OM Marker is generated during any action done to the Network Product. Provide OM Marker is generated when the Network Product is added to the order. Change OM Marker is generated when the Network Product in the service is changed within the order. Cease OM Marker is generated when the Network Product is being ceased. Figure 41: OM Marker to Network Product / NPP Mapping Table (OP_OM_MARKER_GEN_NWPDT) In the mapping table above, the OM Marker (“NREGPT”) is mapped to the “Port Speed” NPP of Network Product (“CNP0001”). With the Network Product Action tagged as “Change”, this implies that when the “Port Speed” NPP is modified from the service image in a Change order, this OM Marker will be generated regardless of the new value of this NPP. Similarly, OM Marker “NCP1PL” is mapped to the Network Product “CNP0001”, and not any other NPP. This implies that once this Network Product is triggered, the OM Marker will be generated without any further checks against any other conditions. OM Markers to Order Conditions Figure 42: Illustration of Adding Order Level OM Markers OM Markers can also be mapped to order-level conditions. In these cases, the OM Marker will be generated upon the fulfilment of the pre-defined order-level conditions. This is generally independent of any Network Products nor NPPs. Entity Name Entity Description Rule ID Unique identifier of this rule Service Type Defines the service type that is associated to this OM marker OM Marker Indicates the OM Marker that is mapped to this rule Column Name Indicates the target table and column that this rule is applied towards Column Value Indicates the condition to be fulfilled defined for this rule Status Indicates the status of this rule. Status Status Description 1 Active 2 Inactive Table Name Indicates the tables that will form the SQL statement for the “FROM” Where Clause Indicates the conditions forming the “WHERE” clause of the SQL statement. Figure 43: Order Level OM Marker Rule Definition Table (OP_OM_MARKER_GEN_ORD) The above shows the rule definition captured in the rule definition table. In the above example, and for the specific Service Type, the OM Marker “ECNETE” is generated when the specific condition defined within the rule is fulfilled. To evaluate the criteria, an SQL statement is formed via the following extracts. SELECT FROM WHERE Once evaluated, if the result set meets the targeted condition as indicated in the “Column Value”, the condition will be considered as fulfilled, and the OM Marker will be generated. OM Markers to Service Image Conditions Another alternative way of configuring the generation of OM Markers is through association to both the Network Product selected during the order and the Network Product currently instanced in the service. Entity Name Entity Description Rule ID Unique identifier of this rule Selected Network Product Indicates the Network Product that the defined OM Marker is associated to Instanced Network Product Indicates the NPP that is mapped to the condition required to generate the defined OM Marker When the value is null, it indicates the OM Marker will be generated regardless of conditions. OM Marker Indicates the OM Marker that is mapped to this rule Service Type Defines the service type that is associated to this OM marker Order Type Indicates the order type of which this rule will be applicable for. Order Type Order Type Description 1 Provide 2 Change 3 Cease Figure 44: Service Condition OM Marker Rule Definition Table (OP_NW_MARKER_GEN_ADD) The above shows the rule definitions captured in the service condition rule definition table. For a given rule, it evaluates if the service contains the Network Product as defined in the “Instanced Network Product”. After which, it then checks if the order selected contains the defined “Selected Network Product” before generating the defined OM Marker.

title: Singtel Spring R2 ESOM High Level Design v2.16.docx - Activities
content: Activities Figure 45: ESOM Activity Table Screengrab The figure above shows a series of activities within ESOM being generated to form a single workflow. Activities are defined as the various individual steps or instructions, collectively known as a provisioning flow, necessary for the fulfilment of an order. Through the OM Marker mapping to Activities definition, a set of Activities can then be derived with the generated OM Markers. Entity Name Entity Description Activity ID Unique identifier of this Activity Service Type Defines the service type that is associated to this Activity Order Type Indicates the order type of which this Activity will be applicable for. Order Type Order Type Description 1 Provide 2 Change 3 Cease Activity Type Defines if an Activity is automated or manual Activity Type Activity Type Description A Automated M Manual Activity Description Description of the Activity Activity Name Short Name of this Activity Activity Owner The user who owns this Activity Queue Jeopardy Hours Defines the number of hours beyond an Activity’s Required By Date (RBD) from which an Activity goes into jeopardy state Jeopardy Minutes Defines the number of minutes beyond an Activity’s Required By Date (RBD) from which an Activity goes into jeopardy state Activity Mnemonic Defines any additional details for this Activity Activity Mnemonic Description Purpose 000000001 Effective Activity For Job Effective Date (JED) calculation CABJUMPER CABJUMPER Defined as “Installation Activity” to be sent to ESMs. IPTVSTB IPTVSTB Defined as “Installation Activity” to be sent to ESMs. MCONFIG MCONFIG Defined as “Installation Activity” to be sent to ESMs. OPO OPO Defined as “Outside Plant Operations” PCCONFIG PCCONFIG Defined as “Installation Activity” to be sent to ESMs. PCINSTALL PCINSTALL Defined as “Installation Activity” to be sent to ESMs. RMTCONFIG RMTCONFIG Defined as “Installation Activity” to be sent to ESMs. STSURVEY STSURVEY Defined as “Installation Activity” to be sent to ESMs. ZDT ZDT Defined as “Installation Activity” to be sent to ESMs. NA No additional detailed defined. Provisioning Indicator Defines if this Activity is the critical step during the provisioning process. Provisioning Indicator Description Y Yes N No Auto Class Name This is only applicable for automated activities. Defines the name of the auto class to be triggered when this activity is generated. Activity Category Defines the category for this Activity Activity Category Description A Exchange Work (Analogue) B Special Billing Arrangements D Default E Auto-Com Without External Interfaces F Exchange Work TD (Repairs) G Exchange Work RC (Repairs) I Installation (Field Works) J Installation (Allocator Review) L Pair Allocation (Checking) M Teleview Marketing N Number Allocation O Exchange Work P Pair Allocation S System Generated X Exchange Jumpering Work Y Payphone Work Z Advance Payment Status Indicates the status of this Activity configuration. Status Status Description 1 Active 2 Inactive Figure 46: Activity Definitions Table (OM_ACT_MASTER) The above illustrates how Activities can be configured in ESOM. All Activities are configured within the activity definitions table. Activities are associated to a Service Type, and can be uniquely identified within the Service Type via the Activity ID.

title: Singtel Spring R2 ESOM High Level Design v2.16.docx - Activity Required By Date
content: Activity Required By Date Each Activity has a deadline (required by date) that defines when an Activity must be completed by. If an Activity’s required by date has lapsed, the Activity would have been determined to be delayed. Entity Name Entity Description Activity ID Unique identifier of this Activity Service Type Defines the service type that is associated to this Activity Order Type Indicates the order type of which this Activity will be applicable for Order Type Order Type Description 1 Provide 2 Change 3 Cease Relative Time Defines the amount of time allowed to lapse to derive the required by date. (e.g. -1, 0, 1, 2, etc.) Relative Time Unit Defines the unit of time that the relative time is calculated with. Relative Time Unit Time Unit Description 1 Day 2 Hour 3 Minute Relative Time To Defines the basis where the required by date will be calculated against. Relative Time To Relative Time To Description ADV Advance Appointment Date APT Appointment Date CRD Customer Required Date OPO OPO (FTTH) Appointment Date ORD Order Issued Date SSY Site Survey (FTTH) STD System Trigger Date OM Marker Defines the presence of this OM Marker from which this rule is valid When OM Marker is labelled as “S00001”, this implies that this dependency is applicable for all scenarios, regardless of OM Markers Status Indicates the status of this relative time rule. Status Status Description 1 Active 2 Inactive Figure 47: Relative Time Definitions Table (OM_RELATIVE_TIME) The above illustrates how an Activity’s required by date can be configured. title: Singtel Spring R2 ESOM High Level Design v2.16.docx - Activity Dependency
content: Activity Dependency Figure 48: Illustration of a Provisioning Flow In a provisioning flow generated within ESOM, some Activities can only be performed after a pre-requisite Activity is completed. In the above illustration, Activity 3 is dependent on the completion of Activities 1 and 2 before it can be worked on. As such, Activities in ESOM can be configured to have pre-requisites and dependencies. This establishment of Activity dependencies validates that all pre-requisite Activities have been completed before an Activity is performed. Activities can only be dependent on other Activities that exist within the same order, and not across multiple work orders. Entity Name Entity Description Activity ID Unique identifier of this Activity Service Type Defines the service type that is associated to this Activity Order Type Indicates the order type of which this Activity will be applicable for. Order Type Order Type Description 1 Provide 2 Change 3 Cease Predecessor Activity ID Defines the Activity that is a pre-requisite to this Activity. OM Marker Defines the presence of this OM Marker from which this dependency is valid When OM Marker is labelled as “S00001”, this implies that this dependency is applicable for all scenarios, regardless of OM Markers Status Indicates the status of this dependency rule. Status Status Description 1 Active 2 Inactive Figure 49: Activity Dependency Definitions Table (OM_ACT_DEPEND) The figure above shows how an Activity dependency can be configured within the dependency definitions table. Activity dependencies are an optional type of entity that can be configured to an Activity. An Activity can have no dependencies, or can have one or more dependencies configured to them.

title: Singtel Spring R2 ESOM High Level Design v2.16.docx - OM Group
content: OM Group OM Group are the various provisioning teams with access to ESOM. Each OM Group is responsible to perform on the Activities assigned to them. Each group shall be defined in the group definition table, as described below. Entity Name Entity Description Group ID Unique identifier of this Group Group Description Brief description of this Group Group Owner Defines the owner of this Group Department Code Defines the department that this Group is under Group ID Email Defines the email address from which notifications to this Group will be sent to Batch Print Indicator Indicates if this Group has permissions to batch print work orders assigned to them Batch Print Indicator Description Y Yes N No Status Indicates the status of this Group Status Status Description 1 Active 2 Inactive Figure 52: OM Group Definitions Table (OM_GRP)
