title: Singtel Spring R2 ESOM High Level Design v2.16.docx - Order Submission
content: Order Submission Overview ESOM is accepting order request from ECOM and ESOM Order Broker at Work Order level as illustrated below. Each order request contains one and only one Work Order with its associated Service Order number. Figure 65: Order Request Payload acceptable by ESOM Below illustrates an end-to-end view of how a Service Order with multiple Work Orders are submitted from ECOM and pushed down to ESOM. After a Service Order is submitted into ESOM, ESOM will be performing two levels of validation before the fulfilment process can proceed. Throughout the validation and fulfilment process, ESOM will be sending back Key Status Update (KSU) back to ECOM to notify the fulfilment status of the current Work Order. Both Validation and Fulfilment KSU will be sent on Work Order level. Figure 66: Order Response Payload that ESOM will be responding Below illustrates the interaction diagram for the various KSUs that ESOM will be responding back to ECOM via ESOM OB. Figure 67: Order Submission KSU from ESOM Process Level Status Description 1 Work Order Rejected Work Order submitted to ESOM has failed Level 1 basic validation. Validation includes xsd validation Duplicate ECOM TXN Ids Unsupported Arbor Service Type Esom system error cases 2 Work Order Received Work Order has passed Level 1 validation and ESOM acknowledge the receipt of this Service Order request. 3 Work Order Rejected Work Order submitted to ESOM has failed Level 2 validation. Validation includes Order specific validation Product specific validation 4 Work Order In Progress ESOM has successfully decomposed the Work Order and activities have been generated. Fulfilment process is currently In Progress in ESOM 5 Work Order NPP, Routing Info and Notes have been updated in ESOM, and the updated NPP, Routing Info and Notes will be passed on to ECOM 6 Work Order ESOM has generated JED and JED to be passed on to ECOM as part of this KSU 7 Work Order PONR Work Order has entered Point-of-No-Return state 8 Work Order Completed ESOM has completed the fulfilment process and the Work Order is completed.

title: Singtel Spring R2 ESOM High Level Design v2.16.docx - Order Amendment
content: Order Amendment Overview ESOM supports order amendment as per legacy OM at Work Order level. It is expected for ECOM to send down the amendment details (eg. Updated NPP) together with the updated Work Order details (eg. Updated CRD) in the request payload. Each amendment request to ESOM from Order Taker in ECOM can comprise of one or many amendments to the Work Order. Figure 68: Amendment Request at Work Order Level As ESOM can only process an Amendment Request when the Work Order has persisted successfully into the database, ESOM is expecting ECOM to only send the Amendment Request after ESOM has responded with the “In Progress” KSU as illustrated below. Any attempt to amend a Work Order prior to “In Progress” status in ESOM will be rejected. Figure 69: Amend request to be sent after ESOM has responded with "In Progress" KSU After an amendment request has been submitted into ESOM, ESOM will be performing some validation before commencing on the amendment request. Below illustrates the interaction diagram for the various KSUs that ESOM will be responding back to ECOM. Figure 70: Amendment KSU from ESOM Process Level Status Description 1 Work Order Rejected Work Order Amendment submitted to ESOM has failed Level 1 basic validation. Validation includes xsd validation duplicated amend request checks amend request before ESOM Work Order reaches “In Progress” status ECOM amend Sequence no is not matching with ESOM 2 Work Order Received Work Order Amendment has passed Level 1 validation and ESOM acknowledge the receipt of this Amendment request 3 Work Order Rejected Work Order Amendment submitted to ESOM has failed Level 2 validation. Validation includes Order specific validation (eg. validation of amendment codes) Product specific validation 4 Work Order Amendment In Progress ESOM has started the amendment process 5 Work Order Amended ESOM has successfully amended the Work Order ECOM/ESOM Work Order Amend Number Validation To prevent erroneous overriding of the work order image in ESOM, two new fields called ESOMWorkOrdAmendNo and NPPUpdatedFlag have been introduced. ESOMWorkOrdAmendNo defines the current ESOM Network Product Parameter details version number. Whenever there is an update to ESOM NPP Image by OM User through ESOM Web Portal or by ESOM ESM, ESOMWorkOrdAmendNo will be incremented. This field will be sent back to ECOM as part of the Work Order KSU. NPPUpdatedFlag is a field to be derived by ECOM before amendment request submission. If there’s an update to the NPP during amendment, the field will be populated with a “Y”, else “N”. During Work Order Amendment, ECOM will be sending both fields as part of the order payload to ESOM. ESOM will be performing a L1 Validation to determine whether the ESOMWorkOrdAmendNo is in sync with what is captured in ESOM database. If there is any discrepancy, ESOM will be rejecting the order. This validation will only happen when the NPPUpdatedFlag is populated with “Y”. The rationale for this approach is for amendment to proceed in ESOM when NPP is not updated during ECOM amendment (eg. CRD change) but ESOMWorkOrdAmendNo is out of sync between ECOM and ESOM. Similarly, in ECOM, a validation check will be performed on the WorkOrderAmendSeqNo, if there is any discrepancy, ECOM will fail the validation. Below illustrates some of the scenarios discussed above. Figure 71: Scenario 1: ECOM amendment performed on the latest ESOM image Figure 72: ECOM amendment is not performed on the latest ESOM image Figure 73: NPP is updated on the latest ECOM image in ESOM Figure 74: NPP is not updated on the latest ECOM image in ESOM Fulfilment Flow Below illustrates the high-level fulfilment process of the amendment request from ECOM. Figure 75: High-Level Fulfilment Process for Amendment Request S/N Process Description 1 COM Order Broker will be connecting to the Order Submit Request queue and consuming any incoming amendment request sent by ECOM. 2 Once L1 and L2 validation have passed, COM Order Broker will be persisting the amendment details (including Amendment Codes) into ESOM Database. 3 Amend Work Order BW Process in OM Workflow Engine will be picking up records from the Amend Work Order shadow table and kicking start with the amendment process. 4 Once amendment has been completed, Status Engine within COM Order Broker will then inform ECOM that amendment has been completed via a KSU.

title: Singtel Spring R2 ESOM High Level Design v2.16.docx - Work Order Priority and Designated Queue
content: Work Order Priority and Designated Queue In principle, ECOM will be submitting Orders request and ESOM will be responding back into the corresponding queues based on the priority assigned at the work order level. Order request and response here refer to Order Submission, Order Amendment and Order Cancellation. Below table describes the queue designation logic. S/N Designated Queue Condition 1 orderSubmitReq If any of the Work Order priority of a Service Order falls within “Super Express”, “Express” or “Normal” 2 lowPriorityOrderReq If all the Work Order’s priority of a given Service Order falls within “Low Priority” 3 orderSubmitRes If any of the Work Order priority of a Service Order falls within “Super Express”, “Express” or “Normal” and the response KSU is at Service Order level OR Work Order Priority falls within “Super Express”, “Express” or “Normal” and response KSU is at Work Order level 4 lowPriorityOrderRes If all the Work Order’s priority of a given Service Order falls within “Low Priority” and the response KSU is at Service Order level OR Work Order Priority falls within “Low Priority” and response KSU is at Work Order level To achieve the above logic, a new field called Service Order Priority will be introduced as part of the order payload for ESOM to know what the priority at Service Order Level is. ECOM will derive the value of this field as the highest priority level of all the Work Orders assigned to the Service Order before order is submitted down to ESOM. Below table describes the various scenarios and the designated request and response queue. S/N Service Order Priority Work Order/s Priority Designated Request Queue Designated Response Queue 1 Super Express WO #1: Super Express orderSubmitReq SO KSU: orderSubmitRes WO KSU: orderSubmitRes 2 Express WO #1: Express WO #2: Normal orderSubmitReq SO KSU: orderSubmitRes WO KSU: orderSubmitRes 3 Low Priority WO #1: Low Priority lowPriorityOrderReq SO KSU: lowPriorityOrderRes WO KSU: lowPriorityOrderRes 4 Low Priority WO #1: Low Priority WO #2: Low Priority lowPriorityOrderReq SO KSU: lowPriorityOrderRes WO KSU: lowPriorityOrderRes 5 Super Express WO #1: Super Express WO #2: Express WO #3: Low Priority orderSubmitReq SO KSU: orderSubmitRes WO KSU (Super Express & Express): orderSubmitRes WO KSU (Low Priority): lowPriorityOrderRes For response queue, if there are more than one KSU response pending to send back to ECOM, COM Order Broker – Status Notification Engine will be prioritizing the KSU based on the priority of the work order followed by when is the KSU response event created. title: Singtel Spring R2 ESOM High Level Design v2.16.docx - ESOM Ordering Scenarios
content: ESOM Ordering Scenarios Figure 82: ESOM Order Model with Action Types ESOM maintains the same 2 concepts of Action Types at the Work Order level, “Service Action Type” and “Order Action Type”. Both Action Types are expected to be selected or system populated in ECOM during order capture, and then sent down to ESOM. A combination of both action types will be used to determine ESOM’s provisioning behaviour towards such orders. S/N Service Action Type 1 Normal 2 Transfer SI 3 Retain No 4 TOS 5 unTOS 6 Change Num with Retain Old Num 7 ER Change Order 8 RC 9 2-Way TD 10 ER WITH Retain No 11 ER WITHOUT Retain No S/N Order Action Type 1 Normal 2 Contract Renewal 3 Hot Upgrade 4 Hot Downgrade 5 Parallel Upgrade 6 Parallel Downgrade 7 Parallel ER 8 ConRenew (MS) 9 ISDN - Migration/Conversion Service Action Types are used to identify the business scenario that the customer has requested for, while Order Action Types are used to identify pairs of Work Orders that are required to be raised to fulfil such business needs. In the subsequent sections below, the various combinations of Service and Order Action Types will be shown to illustrate the fulfilment of the corresponding business scenarios. New Service Provisioning Figure 83: Order Illustration for New Provide In the provisioning of a new service, ESOM generates a single Work Order with Service Action Type “Normal”, with each Provide Work Order resulting in the creation of a single service. Modification of Service Figure 84: Illustration of Service Modification When modifying an existing service, a single Change Work Order is required with Service Action Type “Normal”. This is applicable for any addition or removal of VASes, or a modification on the main service itself. TOS Figure 85: Illustration for TOS of Service When raising a Temporary Out of Service (TOS) order, a Change Work Order is required with Service Action Type “TOS”. A TOS Network Product is added as part of the Change order. unTOS Figure 86: Illustration of unTOS of Service Conversely, in an unTOS order, the reverse Service Action Type of “unTOS” is expected to be sent from ECOM. Within the Change Order, the existing TOS Network Product is expected to be ceased. Parallel Upgrade of Service Figure 87: Illustration of Parallel Upgrade In the scenario of Parallel Upgrade, the existing service is expected to be ceased while a new upgrade service is provided. Both the Order Action Type for Cease and Provide Work Orders are “Parallel Upgrade”. This allows for the Provide Work Order to be completed first before the existing service is ceased. Parallel Downgrade of Service Figure 88: Illustration of Parallel Downgrade Conversely, the similar Cease-Provide combination of Work Orders are created for the Parallel Downgrade. The Order Action Type for both Work Orders are “Parallel Downgrade”. Parallel Relocation of Service Figure 89: Illustration of Parallel Relocation For both scenarios of retaining / not retaining the service numbers, a Provide-Cease Work Order combination will be created, with Order Action Type of “Parallel ER” for all the Work Orders. Hot Upgrade of Service Figure 90: Illustration of Hot Upgrade In the event of a Hot Upgrade, a Change Work Order is created against the existing Service, with Order Action Type of “Hot Upgrade”. Hot Downgrade of Service Figure 91: Illustration for Hot Downgrade Conversely for Hot Downgrade, the same Change Work Order is created against the existing Service, marked with Order Action Type of “Hot Downgrade”. Hot Relocation of Service Figure 92: Illustration for Hot Relocation During Hot Relocation, a Normal Change Work Order is generated, while the Service Order Action Type is tagged as “ER Change Order”. Change of Ownership Figure 93: Illustration for Change of Ownership within Customer Account In a Change of Ownership (SI Transfer) scenario, the existing service image is ceased, while a new service is provisioned under the new billing account. This scenario is applicable for SI Transfers within the same Customer Account. Figure 94: Illustration of Change of Ownership across Customer Accounts An alternative scenario for SI Transfer involves the transfer of ownership across different Billing Accounts belong to separate Customer Accounts. In these cases, 2 service orders are created, 1 for the cessation of the existing service under the existing Billing Account, and a second one to the Provide Order for the new Billing Account. Cessation of Service Figure 95: Illustration for Cessation For cessation of an existing service, the Order Action Type for the Cease Order will be marked as “Normal”. The service shall be terminated once the Cease Order is completed.

content: TDRC Request with Switch Provisioning This scenario will be supported in ESOM via a Non-Order flow. No Service Order or Work Order will be generated in ESOM. ESOM will be connecting to the TDRC Request queue residing in ECOM to process the request. Below illustrates the high-level interaction diagram for the TDRC request with switch provisioning. Figure 97: Interaction Diagram of TDRC Request with Switch Provisioning Step Process Description 1 ECOM will be submitting the Non-Order Request to the JMS queue that ESOM COM Order Broker will be connecting to and consuming the message. 2 ESOM will be performing the validation of the payload to make sure the request can be accepted and processed correctly. 3 If any validation fails, ESOM will be sending a failed validation notification back to ECOM. 4 If validation passes, ESOM will sending an acknowledge notification back to ECOM. 5 ESOM will then process the request and send the activation requests to the network activation systems 6 If provisioning is successful, ESOM will sending a completion notification back to ECOM. 7 If provisioning is not successful, ESOM will be sending a failed notification back to ECOM. Supported Service Type Below is the list of supported OP Service Type and Arbor Service Type for this scenario extracted from legacy. Below list is for reference and any discrepancy from legacy shall have the current configuration in legacy production as the source of truth. S/N OP Service Type Arbor Service Type Arbor Service Type Description Supported TD Status Remarks 1 TS 401 TS - DEL TD0, TD2 2 TS 413 TS - MoIP TD0, TD2 3 PT 950 IPTV TD2 4 SG 202 SingNet TD2 Only applicable to “Non-Corp” SingNet products 5 SS 980 SaaS TD2 Excluding ONEOfficeNoFrills products 6 TS 403 TS - PABX TD2 7 TS 404 TS - PhoneNet TD2 8 TS 412 TS - VCall TD2 9 VS 510 VS - Virtual Services TD2 Fulfilment Flow Below illustrates the high-level fulfilment process of the TDRC request with switch provisioning. Figure 98: High Level Fulfilment Process for TDRC request with Switch Provisioning S/N Process Description 1 COM Order Broker will be connecting to the tdrcReq queue and consuming any incoming request sent by ECOM. ESOM is expecting each Non-Order TDRC Request payload to contain only one service to be TDRC-ed. Below illustrate the scenarios supported in ESOM. Figure 99: ECOM supporting a single TD non-order request in each payload 2 COM Order Broker will perform the necessary validation and insert the request record into a staging table. 3 Managed Collection BW process will pick up any new record from the staging table and process the record. Depending on the service type, Managed Collection BW process will route the request to the subsequent BW process or invoke the internal service in JBoss. Service Type Process Telephony Services SoftAct BW Process IPTV Services IPTV BW Process SingNet Services SLMD BW Process SaaS Services ESMActivity EJB 4 SoftAct BW Process will send down the provisioning request to SoftAct network activation system. 5 IPTV BW Process will send down the provisioning request to SoftTV network activation system. 6 SLMD BW Process will send down the provisioning request to MD network activation system. 7 ESMActivity EJB will send down the provisioning request to MyBiz Portal. 8 Upon completion of the TDRC provisioning, Managed Collection BW Process will be updating the Service Status to the corresponding TD Status. Managed Collection BW Process will then update COM Order Broker on the completion of the provisioning. 9 COM Order Broker will notify back to ECOM by sending a response request to the tdrcRes queue.

title: Singtel Spring R2 ESOM High Level Design v2.16.docx - FOB Sharepoint – Obsolete
content: FOB Sharepoint – Obsolete Note : This interface has been discussed and agreed with Singtel to be obsoleted as it is no longer in use Electronic Service Report Form (eSRF) allows the customer to sign on a Tablet PC upon job completion. The eSRF is then published onto a SharePoint server for automatic e-mailing as PDF attachment to the customer. Electronic Site Survey Information Report (eSSIR) form is used by FOB Field Supervisors to fill in details required to inform customer of the results of the site survey. This is to prepare customer of the required support from them. FOB SharePoint interfaces would enable extraction of data to auto-populate certain fields for eSRF and eSSIR forms and COM the order activity in ESOM. This simplifies the manual steps performed by Field Supervisors or Project Officers to retrieve information from ESOM to fill up eSRF and eSSIR forms. ESOM would also process the input files from FOB Sharepoint and COM the relevant activity as specified in the input files. This helps to reduce the manual effort to COM of order activities by Field Supervisors and Project Officers. Figure 115: Integration between ESOM and FOB Sharepoint

title: Singtel Spring R2 ESOM High Level Design v2.16.docx - Key Functionality
content: Key Functionality Below illustrates a high-level flow of the COM Order Broker functionalities. Figure 143: COM Order Broker High-Level functional flow Process Description Order Receipt ECOM Order Processor and ECOM TDRC Processor modules will be responsible to connect to the JMS queue in ECOM EIL and consuming the incoming request messages. Payload will be in XML format and interface specification will be discussed in detail in the ECOM & ESOM Interface Contract. Level 1 Validation Upon successful receipt of the incoming request, Validation engine will be invoked to perform Level 1 validation. Any failed validation will result in ESOM rejecting the order back to ECOM. In general, Level 1 Validation includes XSD validation Duplicate Order/Request check Unsupported Arbor Service Type Level 2 Validation Upon successful Level 1 validation, Level 2 validation will be kicked be in. Any failed validation will result in ESOM rejecting the order back to ECOM. In general, Level 2 Validation includes Order specific validation Product specific validation Persist ECOM request into ESOM Database Once both Level 1 and Level 2 validations have passed, the validation engine will be persisting the ECOM request (eg. Service Order and Work Order entities) into ESOM Database. This is when OM Workflow Engine will be picking up the transaction records to kick start the order decomposition process. Status Notification Status Notification Engine is the module in which a KSU (Key Status Update) will be notified back to ECOM. This module will be connecting to ECOM EIL JMS queue and posting KSU message for ECOM to consume. Status Notification Engine will be informed by COM Order Broker modules as well as OM Workflow Engine modules when there’s a need to notify a KSU back to ECOM.

title: Singtel Spring R2 ESOM High Level Design v2.16.docx - High Level Architecture
content: High Level Architecture Figure 147: High Level Workflow Engine Architecture The workflow engine is an uplifting of the legacy Vitria Projects (such as Job Server and the respective ESM Automator Projects) onto the various TIBCO components. The diagram above shows the overall processing of the workflow engine Process Description 1 The processing in workflow engine starts after the COM Order Broker processing, in which a new work order details would have been persisted into the records in the ESOM database. When this happens, a database trigger would copy the particular work order into a shadow table that acts as a input point for workflow engine to start. 2 There will be two TIBCO BusinessWork processes that monitors the changes into the two main shadow table for the workflow engine one that monitor changes to a work order one that monitor changes to a work order activities. Once it detect a changes in the underlying shadow table, the process will then translate the changes into a message that is posted into incoming JMS queue for the order orchestration engine. 3 Order orchestration engine is the component that orchestrates the complete provisioning activities for a single work order. It will be built on top of TIBCO BusinessEvents (BE), emulating the state-transition processing currently performed by legacy Job Server. Upon receiving the message in the incoming queue, TIBCO BE will translate the message into an event, and process the incoming work order according to the rules configured. Each rules carries out a specific condition on which it should be executed. Once the condition is met, it will be calling imported Java class from ESOM JobServer to carry out the JobServer processing logics. 4 TIBCO Rule Engine processes the incoming events. The processing is basically executing various function, depending on the event received (which can be work order related, or activity of a specific work order). Instantiates TIBCO BE objects at the start. This object instance (a work order) will remain in TIBCO BE until all provisioning activities are completed Initial de-composition of a work order into a sequence of provisioning activities with dependencies Calculate the date and time of when certain provisioning activity should take place, and set a scheduler timer to ensure the specific activity is executed at its scheduled time When a pre-decessor activity is completed, it will flag the subsequent activity as ready for execution 5 If a specific activity requires function calls to an external systems, the rule engine will send an event to an outgoing JMS queue. On the other end of this queue, there are a sets of TIBCO BW process configured to translate the request into sets of API calls to external system. The rule engine also send a request to outgoing queue when it needs an update of the data inside the ESOM database (i.e. insert new activities for a work order, update the status of an activity, etc.) 6 There will be multiple TIBCO BW processes, each configured to interface with a specific external system. Details of each these TIBCO BW process will be discussed in the ESOM Technical Design Document. In addition of interfacing to an external system, there will be BW processes that updates internal tables of workflow in ESOM database, as well as updates to the work order and activity table as mentioned in step 5. 7 Once a specific activity is completed, BW process might update the underlying work order and activity table and/or send a message to inform back to the order orchestration engine. When the underlying table is updated by BW process, the existing database triggers outlined in step 1 will kicks in, and the processing will repeat again from step 1 until all activities of a work order have all been completed.

title: Singtel Spring R2 ESOM High Level Design v2.16.docx - Order Orchestration Engine
content: Order Orchestration Engine Activity Management Figure 148: Illustration of sample Workflow with Activities Once OM Workflow Engine receives the order request from COM Order Broker, ESOM kicks off the process of order decomposition and Activity generation, before combining the set of Activities to form a workflow. Activity Lifecycle Figure 149: Activity Lifecycle (Flows) Figure 150: Activity Lifecycle (Table) Each Activity within ESOM will have a lifecycle. Activities will be first generated as “Not Ready” (NRD) and will end as either “Completed” (COM) or “Cancelled” (CAN). S/N Activity Lifecycle Status Activity Description 1 Not Ready (NRD) This status is set during order decomposition once the Activity is generated. The Activity will remain in NRD status until all its dependencies (if applicable) are either COM or CAN. 2 Ready (RDY) This status is set when an Activity has no dependencies, or when all its dependencies are either COM or CAN. 3 Delayed (DLY) This status is set when an Activity’s RBD has elapsed. 4 Deleted (DEL) This status is set when an Activity is deleted. 5 Cancelled (CAN) This status is set when the Activity has been deleted successfully, or when the Work Order has been cancelled. 6 Executed SoftAct (EXCSFT) This status is applicable only for automated Activities that are sent to SoftAct. This status is set when the Activity has been sent to SoftAct. 7 Executing (EXC) This status is set when an Activity is being executed upon. 8 Completed (COM) This status is set when an Activity is completed. Figure 151: Activity Status Definition Activity Deadline During the fulfilment process, each Activity that is generated will be set with an Activity deadline, known technically as the Required-By Date (RBD), which indicates the date that the Activity needs be completed for the order to be fulfilled in time. Deadline Configuration S/N Activity ID Relative Time Relative Time Unit Relative Time To 1 A 0 Days ORD 2 B 2 Days ORD 3 C -5 Days APT 4 D -1 Days APT 5 E -1 Days APT 6 F -2 Hours APT 7 G 0 Days CRD 8 H 0 Days CRD Figure 152: Sample Configurations from Relative Time Definitions (OM_RELATIVE_TIME) To support the Activity deadlines as listed in the example above, the figure above illustrates how these Activities can be configured via the Relative Time definitions table. They can be interpreted as such. AFTER e.g. ID 1: -5 Days AFTER Appointment Date As Activity deadlines are time sensitive, they can be configured in hourly blocks (e.g. 2 hours before Appointment Date). In the event that the Activity deadline is configured in daily blocks, the time that an Activity’s deadline is set against will be defaulted to 12am, on the day of the date. Deadline Reference Dates The comparative dates (identified via the Relative Time To column in the above table) are necessary for ESOM to derive the Activity deadline needs to be captured as part of the order needs and sent down from ECOM. The figure below describes the types of dates that are required for each scenario. Date Type Condition Description ADV Advance Appointment Date Date of which an Advance Appointment is booked for. This is only applicable for Work Orders with appointments, and with an appointment description of “DEL Advance Wiring”. APT Appointment Date Date of which an Appointment is booked. This is only applicable for Work Orders with appointments, and for all appointment descriptions other than of “DEL Advance Wiring” and “OPO”. CRD Customer Required Date Date of which the Customer has requested for the service to be ready by for each Work Order. OPO OPO (FTTH) Appointment Date Date of which the FTTH Appointment is booked. This is only applicable for Work Orders with appointments, and with an appointment description of “OPO”. ORD Order Issued Date Date of which the service order is submitted. SSY Site Survey (FTTH) Date of which the Site Survey Appointment is booked. This is only applicable for Work Orders with appointments, and with an appointment requested type of “Survey”. STD System Triggered Date Date of which this Activity is triggered by ESOM. Figure 153: Conditions to Determine RBD After the process Activity generation completes, ESOM will then generate and assign the Activity deadlines for each Activity based on the various dates sent down from ECOM. Deadline Amendment Activity deadlines can be amended during the provisioning process from ESOM Web Portal. A series of verification will be conducted before the Activity deadline can be amended. S/N Verification Type Verification Description 1 User Permission Verifies if the user has the permission to amend the Activity deadline. Users with this permission are configured within the following with KEY_TY: 2 Activity Name Verifies if the Activity’s deadline can be amended. This verification is done against the Service Type and Order Type. This is configured within the following. with KEY_TY: 3 Activity Status Verifies if the Activity status is already marked as “Completed” or “Cancelled” 4 Group IDs Verifies if amendment is valid for Group ID routed to this Activity. This is a 2-step verification with the following. with KEY_TY: with KEY_TY: (from Step 1) 5 New Deadline Verifies if the new Activity deadline entered is valid. The verification steps are: New deadline must be before CRD New deadline must be equal to or after current date The Activity deadline for Successor Activities after the current one must be equal to or later than the new deadline New deadline must be equal to or after any predecessor Activity’s deadline Figure 154: New Deadline Verification Logic Once all 5 verification criteria have been passed, only then the new Activity deadline can be accepted, and the Activity details updated as per the requested amendment. Delay and Jeopardy Figure 155: Work Orders in Jeopardy After an Activity’s RBD has elapsed, the Activity status will be updated to “Delayed” (DLY). Once that occurs, the Jeopardy process will be started. S/N Activity ID Jeopardy Hours Jeopardy Minutes 1 A 0 0 2 B 2 0 3 C 0 0 4 D 1 0 5 E 1 0 6 F 0 0 7 G 2 30 8 H 0 0 Figure 156: Sample Jeopardy Definitions Jeopardy is an escalation mechanism that can be configured against an Activity. Once an Activity goes into Jeopardy, the entire Work Order will be set as Jeopardy. Escalation actions can then be configured against each Activity’s OM Group to process and expediate the resolution of such Work Orders. Activity Completion Date Once an Activity has been assigned to an OM Group, the various parties assigned to that OM Group will be responsible for performing the various fulfilment steps. Upon performing their tasks, they will then move to complete (“COM”) the Activity within ESOM. An Activity can be completed in ESOM via the following channels. For manual Activities performed by OM Users, these Activities can be manually COM via the ESOM Web UI. For manual Activities that are picked up by OM Batch jobs, ESOM’s batch framework will process and COM these Activities. For manual Activities that are expected to be COM by an external system, the various ESMs will be expected to invoke ESOM’s API to COM these Activities. For automated Activities that are assigned to autoclasses, ESOM’s internal processes will process and COM these Activities. On each Activity, the Activity Completion Date would be identified and captured once these Activities are completed. Job Effective Date Figure 157: Illustration of JED Derivation Based on the illustration above, Activity 7: 1036 has been defined as the PI Activity and is the only (and last) PI Activity within the order. As such, the “COM” date of this Activity is determined to also be the JED and is sent back to ECOM. As each Work Order can have varying combinations of Activities, depending on the order image and Network Products sent from the upstream enterprise order capture system, the logic for deriving the JED in ESOM considers the variances between the various Work Orders, and follows a prioritization concept to determine which logic should be applicable. Each Work Order will only have 1 JED generated, and this process of determining JED (when applicable) will be run after each Activity is completed. Priority Condition 1 Completed Date of the Last PI Activity For Work Orders containing a PI Activity (defined as Provisioning Indicator “Y” in the Activity definition table), the completion date of the last PI Activity will be taken as the JED. 2 CRD Date for Immediate Closure Orders For Work Orders marked as Immediate Closure, no PI Activities will be generated. As such, Customer Required Date (CRD) will be taken as the JED. 3 Last Completed Date of Activity For Work Orders that are not Immediate Closure and have no PI Activities, ESOM then checks for Activities configured with “Effective Activity” (defined as Activity Mnemonic “000000001”). The completion date of this Effective Activity is then taken as the JED. If there are multiple Effective Activities, the last Effective Activity to be completed shall be used. 4 For All Other Conditions In the event that none of the above conditions are valid, the completed date of the last Activity will be taken as the JED. Figure 158: JED Logic Determination Priority Point of no Return (PONR) Figure 159: Illustration of Order Progression Point-of-no-Return (PONR) is defined as a point within a Work Order’s provisioning process, where a Work Order has reached a stage where no further amendments nor cancellations can be made to the Work Order. Across all Work Orders, they pass through a series of stages from which PONR is set for the various order types. Stage Provide Order Change Order Cease Order A No restrictions are applied. All order amendments and cancellations allowed. Not PONR Not PONR Not PONR B Amendment allowed for: CRD Appointments Notes No amendment allowed Amendment allowed for: CRD Appointments Notes No cancellation No cancellation No cancellation Partial PONR Partial PONR Partial PONR C Amendment allowed for: CRD Appointments Notes No amendment allowed No amendment allowed No cancellation No cancellation No cancellation Partial PONR PONR PONR D No amendment allowed No amendment allowed No amendment allowed No cancellation No cancellation No cancellation PONR PONR PONR Figure 160: Stage Progression towards PONR The above showcases the various stages a Work Order progresses through before reaching PONR. Partial PONR is an implicit state that is not stored explicitly in any of the transactional tables. ESOM derives the Partial PONR status internally when required (e.g. during amendment validation, new Activity deadline validation, etc.). Once PONR is reached, no forms of alteration / amendments to the Work Order will be possible. If there are any changes required to the service image after PONR, a separate “Change” order should be raised to modify. Immediate Closure Immediate Closure is a behavior which can be set to a Work Order. Once the Work Order has been set as Immediate Closure by Order Taker during order capture in ECOM, most activation Activities will be suppressed apart from a defined set of exceptions. S/N Exceptional Group ID 1 FRMS_FULL 2 MCONF 3 SYSBILLING Figure 161: Exceptional Groups for Immediate Closure The figure above illustrates the exceptional Group IDs from which Activities generated for them would not be suppressed during Immediate Closure (from with KEY_TY: ). These Activities will still be generated and follow the normal provisioning behaviour, as per non-immediate closure Work Orders. Once the Work Order has been marked as Immediate Closure, they will be completed within ESOM almost immediately. Immediate Closure can be potentially used for the following scenarios. Transfer of SI from one billing account to another Raising of backdated orders when provisioning has already been completed prior outside of ESOM ESOM will generate a generic automated Activity and is for the purpose of generating the JED. Referencing the JED derivation logic, the JED of such Work Orders shall be set as the CRD.

title: Singtel Spring R2 ESOM High Level Design v2.16.docx - ESOM Batch Architecture
content: ESOM Batch Architecture Below illustrates the high-level ESOM Batch Architecture. Figure 166: ESOM Batch Architecture Components Description Control-M ESOM will be leveraging on Singtel Control-M for batch scheduling. Control-M is a workload automation software to schedule batch processes on a daily, weekly, or monthly interval. It can also be configured to respond to trigger events (called through API, invocation on demand with Java, etc). It allows batch processes monitoring from a single point of control. Batch Job Shell Script Batch Job shell scripts invoke the command to trigger the Spring Batch. They consist of Job Run Scripts. Spring Batch Spring Batch is the framework which triggers job processing logic driven by job specific configuration file. This configuration file lists the steps to perform and the dependency between the steps. Example of steps include: Clean up working directory to delete stale files Create job request message and send to Job request Queue (which is picked by the Batch Job Process). Wait for response from the Batch Job Process Rename output files if required FTP/SFTP the output file to the destination server Move the output file to the archive directory. Post-run cleanup Bash Script/Java Code Bash script and/or Java code (in the form of JAR) contain the actual logic for batch processes to perform operations required to support ESOM functions. These would be ported from the legacy code base with minimal changes to adhere to ESOM scope.

title: Singtel Spring R2 ESOM High Level Design v2.16.docx - Order Closure
content: Order Closure Figure 168: Order Closure Processes Order closure is a process of clean-up and service instantiation after a Work Order has been completed. This is the final step of a Work Order before it is marked as “Closed” There are 3 stages to order closure, namely, Pre-Closure Validation Service Instantiation SI COM Process Pre-Closure Validation Before the order closure process begins, a set of validations will be conducted to determine each orders’ eligibility for closure. The details are as below. Validation Type Order Type Validation Description Validation Criteria Related Orders Provide For related orders of “Cease-Provide”, the Cease order will have to be closed first before the Provide order can be closed. Applicable for the following Service Action Types: Retain Number ER with Retain Number ER without Retain Number Change Number with Retain Old Number Preceding Orders Change For Change orders, the previous provide order must first be closed before the Change order can be closed. Applicable for all Change orders Preceding Orders Cease For Cease orders, any previous Provide and Change orders must first be closed before the Cease Applicable for all Cease orders NPP Validation All For all orders, the service number must be populated. Applicable for all orders types for all products Figure 169: Pre-Closure Validation Criteria Once the order passes the pre-closure validation across the various order types as stated above, the order is eligible for closure, and goes through the process of Service Instantiation. Service Instantiation Figure 170: Illustration of Service Instantiation Once the Work Order has been validated that it is ready to be closed, it then goes through the process of Service Instantiation. ESOM will transfer the information from the various Work Order transactional tables into the service instance, and ultimately close the Work Order. S/N Type of Data Transactional Table Service Table 1 Network Product OP_NW_ORD_TXN OP_NW_PRDT 2 Network Product Parameter OP_NW_ORD_PARA OP_NW_PRDT_PARA 3 External ID OP_WKO_ORD_EXT_SI_ID_MAP OP_EXT_SI_ID_MAP 4 Address OP_WORK_ORD_ADDR_MAP OP_SVC_INST_ADDR_MAP Figure 171: Conversion of Transactional Data to Service Data As part of Service Instantiation, these sets of data identified in the table above will be transferred from the Work Order to the service image. S/N Entity Table Name Update Description 1 Service Instance OP_SVC_INST Update status for Service instances Provide: Update status from “New” to “Active” Cease: Populate Disconnect Code for existing record Populate Disconnect Reason for existing record For all Order Types, update the Switch Unit if applicable. 2 Work Order OP_WORK_ORD Update status from “Completed” to “Closed” 3 Service Order OP_SVC_ORD Update status from “Completed” to “Closed” 4 Trunk Group ID OP_PORT_NO Update status for Trunk Group IDs in SIP Trunk Orders Provide: Update status from “Spare” to “Working” Cease: Update status from “Working” to “Spare” 5 Project Tie OP_PROJECT Populate End Date for existing record if all Work Orders within the Project are marked as “Closed” 6 Service Tie OP_PRDT_TIE Populate End Date for existing record if all Services within the Product Tie are marked as “Inactive” 7 Service Instance External ID OP_EXT_SI_ID_MAP Update the External ID based on the following scenarios. Provide: Insert new record Change: Insert new record if Network Product with External ID is provided Populate End Date if Network Product with External ID is ceased Update External ID if Network Product with External ID is changed Cease: Populate End Date for existing record 8 Service Instance Address OP_SVC_INST_ADDR_MAP Update the Service Address based on the following scenarios. Provide: Insert new record Change: Update existing record Cease: Populate End Date for existing record 9 Network Product OP_NW_PRDT Update the Network Products based on the following scenarios. Provide: Insert new record Change: Insert new record if Network Product is provided Populate End Date for existing record if Network Product is ceased Cease: Populate End Date for existing record 10 Network Product Parameter OP_NW_PRDT_PARA Update the Network Product Parameters based on the following scenarios. Provide: Insert new record Change: Insert new record if Network Product is provided Populate End Date for existing record if Network Product is ceased Cease: Populate End Date for existing record Figure 172: Updates after Service Instantiation Apart from the tables identified, updates to the transaction tables are also processed to illustrate the completion of Service Instantiation and order closure. The process ends once the corresponding tables stated in the figure above has been updated. SI COM Process Figure 173: SI COM Process After the Service Instantiation process, ESOM will then update the inventory statuses into NGNIS. This process is known as SI COM. The updates to NGNIS are necessary for the following processes: Updating of Number inventory to “Working” Releasing of Number inventory Updating of Routing and EET inventory to “Working” Releasing of Routing and EET inventory Add pairing for N1-N2 number Remove pairing for N1-N2 number Adding Number to MBG and BBG Removing Number from MBG and BBG Adding Number to Intercom shortcode Removing Number from Intercom shortcode Once the resources have been released in NGNIS, they go through the quarantine process and will be available for selection again.

title: Singtel Spring R2 ESOM High Level Design v2.16.docx - Web Portal Architecture
content: Web Portal Architecture ESOM Web Application will be implemented using various technologies. Below illustrates the high-level architecture of ESOM Web Portal. Figure 174: High-Level Architecture of ESOM Web Portal Component Sub Component Description Web Component UI Style All web application requires some UI styles create a consistent look and feel. In OM Web Bootstrap CSS is used for UI styles. It is a framework for HTML, CSS and JavaScript. Web Component Brower Script In OM Web, browser script using jQuery framework. The script and CSS would reside in separate locations, which could be referenced from JSP to achieve the modularity. For instance, the scripts would be placed in a “scripts” folder and accessed in JSPs. In web application structure, we would place the JS and CSS files, including graphics such as images, in “webapp” folder. Web Component Common UI Templates All the webpages will hold some common templates to reflect the same theme, font, style, header, footer, menus, etc. The application is set to follow a specific template for all the controls to maintain professional look and feel of the UI. As a rule of thumb, the header/footer, dashboard, navigation and menus will follow a common template web page. These templates are created using JSP/JS based on the requirement and can be reused in all the pages wherever applicable. Web Component UI Screens The UI screens are the one where the end user can interact with the system through various requests. The UI templates are included in the screens to maintain the theme of the web pages. Apart from common templates, the UI isolates itself based on the requirement and functionalities. In OM Web, the UI screens are designed using JSP which in turn incorporate the features of JS and CSS. Web Component Common UI Templates ESOM Web User Interface is implemented using bootstrap framework. Bootstrap framework is an open-source styling framework for HTML5, CSS and JavaScript. Basic form validation to enhance user experience will be performed in this layer. Web Component Form Object Form Object is a property of the document object. This corresponds to an HTML input form constructed with the tag. A form can be submitted by calling the JavaScript submit method or clicking the form submit button. A JSP may have multiple forms based on the functionalities. Web Component Controller Controller acts on both model and view. It controls the data flow into model object and updates the view whenever data changes. It acts as an routing between View and Model. Controller intercepts all the incoming requests. It keeps view and model separate. As per OM Web architecture, the Controller passes the Form Objects to the Business Façade/Service. Domain Object Domain Object Domain objects are mostly represented by entities and value objects. Generally, most objects that live in domain layer contribute to the model and are domain objects. Here the domain objects are nothing but data holders. There is no business logic in it , where business and/or data access logic is separated from data holders (in other words, Transfer Objects or Value Objects). Here we use the POJO domain objects and the same has been defined in the spring XML configuration as beans . Service Component Business Service Layer This is where the business logic for the application gets implemented. The data from the request get manipulated and the result will be passed to another Business Class for further processing or to the integration layer for fetching data from the ESOM DB. This will be the layer as well to Integrate with VDS through LDAP invocation to authenticate user credentials against Singtel Active Directory (AD). Invoke OM Service Layer internal webservice to integrate with NGNIS Invoke Workflow Engine – Integration Engine internal webservice to integrate with ECM to upload document. Service Component Data Layer This is the data layer that will integrate with ESOM database. Hibernate ORM framework will be used to facilitate this integration. It is a Java framework that simplifies the development of Java application to interact with the database. Common Component Application Logging In ESOM Web Portal, log4j2 logging framework will be used to perform any application logging. Common Component Exception Logging In the event of exceptions in the application, an exception message will be posted to ESOM internal queue on TIBCO EMS and the common logger engine will log a record into ESOM database. Common Component Audit Logging For audit trail logging, an audit message will be posted to ESOM internal queue on TIBCO EMS and the common logger engine will log a record into ESOM database.

title: Singtel Spring R2 ESOM High Level Design v2.16.docx - Portal Security Access
content: Portal Security Access Below describes the various level of security access for ESOM Web Portal. Level Security Type Description 1 ESOM Web Portal deployed within Singtel Internal Network ESOM OM Web is intended to be accessed within Singtel internal network and not accessible directly via the Internet. Figure 175: ESOM Web Portal Access 2 User authentication in ESOM and Singtel AD In order to login successfully into ESOM Web Portal, User must be a valid user configured in ESOM TA_USER table (No password authentication is performed) ESOM User logging into ESOM Web Portal will have their credentials authenticated in Singtel Active Directory (AD). This is achieved in ESOM through the integration with VDS. VDS serves as a binding intermediary, to establish the connection between ESOM and Singtel Active Directory. Figure 176: User authentication in ESOM and Singtel AD 3 User role to screen function mapping Once user has been authenticated successfully and logged in into ESOM Web Portal, the user role that the user has been assigned to will determine which screen functions that the user will have access to. OM Roles comprises Supervisor Performer Controller Viewer Administrator Contractor 5 User Security Group User can also be assigned to zero or many security group/s to determine what kind of security access has been imposed on the screen for the user. Refer to Section on Security Group for more details.

message_processing_system.name: Message Processing System (MPS)
message_processing_system.purpose: Calculates usage charges for customers and sometimes foreign accounts
tasks: Collect usage files from a network mediation layer
Parse each file to determine type, time, duration, and other properties of usage events
Guide each usage event to an Amdocs Kenan or external account
Rate each usage event and store the usage charge and related information in the database
Export rated usage events for foreign carriers and reseller usage events

features: Supports multiple combinations of rating attributes
Allows input in one unit and rating in a different unit
Supports minimum charge and per-unit charge configuration
Supports pre-rated usage to be re-rated or loaded without applying additional charges

billing_and_discounts.standard_processing: During invoice processing, discounts and allowances are applied to usage collected in the current billing run, even if the usage is late.
billing_and_discounts.late_usage_behavior: Late usage from a previous month consumes allowance from the current month by default.

special_late_usage_handling.description: Supports configuration to apply discounts based on the event transaction date instead of the billing date.
impact: Recalculates discounts applied to previous invoices
Generates discount and allowance adjustments when reassessment occurs

notifications.purpose: Allows service providers to track spending across thresholds and usage profiles

The rating engine uses a sophisticated model based on customer and product offering characteristics, while supporting in-line promotions and charge monitoring for notification purposes. The engine delivers high performance and supports diverse interpretations of chargeable events.

message_processing_system.name: Message Processing System (MPS)
message_processing_system.purpose: Calculates usage charges for customers and sometimes foreign accounts
tasks: Collect usage files from a network mediation layer
Parse each file to determine type, time, duration, and other properties of usage events
Guide each usage event to an Amdocs Kenan or external account
Rate each usage event and store the usage charge and related information in the database
Export rated usage events for foreign carriers and reseller usage events

features: Supports multiple combinations of rating attributes
Allows input in one unit and rating in a different unit
Supports minimum charge and per-unit charge configuration
Supports pre-rated usage to be re-rated or loaded without applying additional charges

billing_and_discounts.standard_processing: During invoice processing, discounts and allowances are applied to usage collected in the current billing run, even if the usage is late.
billing_and_discounts.late_usage_behavior: Late usage from a previous month consumes allowance from the current month by default.

special_late_usage_handling.description: Supports configuration to apply discounts based on the event transaction date instead of the billing date.
impact: Recalculates discounts applied to previous invoices
Generates discount and allowance adjustments when reassessment occurs

notifications.purpose: Allows service providers to track spending across thresholds and usage profiles

  "3.           Kenan System Overview": {
    "Kenan Module List": "Billing
Singtel Billing includes the 26 Bill cycles in a month starting from 1st (Billing execution starts from 3rd of the month)  from every month to 26th/27th of the Month. We have 3 types of billing in Singtel in a day.
Cyclic Billing 
This is scheduled Bill cycles for the day like M01, C01, R01 etc. 
Non-Cyclic Billing 
Non-Cycle Billing includes the interim bills and fallout/catch up cases for previous Bill cycles.
Proforma Billing
Proforma Billing is to validate some test bills  before the final bill cycle.
Bill Processing
Bill processing comprises of stream of jobs. However, this document only focuses on four jobs:
BIP Initialization
Script for BIP Execution
Post BIP Error Detection Script
Script to dump BBCQ and BIU – before bill run
Script to dump BBCQ and BIU – after bill run
These four jobs are part of the Bill Cycle (Cyclic and Non-cyclic) Processing Stream. The flow is illustrated below:
The other jobs in the Bill Cycle Processing Stream will not be documented here. However, this document will address the guideline/standard of designing jobs to be run in the Bill Cycle Processing Stream. 
For more details on Billing. Please refer the BFDD document as below.  Latest JPS also attached for reference.
Rating
Amdocs Kenan supports file-based offline rating for post-paid subscribers. The rating engine supports a sophisticated model based on customer and product offering characteristics as well as admitting in-line promotions and charge monitoring for notification purposes. The engine delivers high performance and supports diverse interpretations of chargeable events. 
The Message Processing System (MPS) calculates usage charges for customers (and in some cases for foreign accounts as well). MPS performs the following tasks
Batch Usage Processing Flow
Collects usage files from a network mediation layer.
Parses each file to determine the type, time, duration, and other properties of corresponding usage events. 
Guides each usage event to an Amdocs Kenan or external account. 
Rates each usage event and stores the usage charge and related information in the database.
Exports out collects (rated usage events for foreign carriers) and reseller usage events.
Usage can be rated based on duration, volume, location, time of day, jurisdiction, zone class, distance band, bill class, provide class, type of product, equipment class code, service code and many more attributes and combinations. It’s possible to have inputs in one unit and rating in different units. For each charge, minimum and per unit charges can be also defined. Amdocs Kenan also supports pre-rated usage to be re-rated or loaded without applying additional charges.
In normal invoice processing, discounts and allowance are applied on usage collected during the current bill run, regardless if it’s late or not. In such a case, a late call from a previous month will consume allowance of the current month. Amdocs Kenan also supports special late usage handling through configuration which allows late usage needs to be discounted based on the month it belongs to (event transaction date) and re-calculate related discounts applied to previous invoices. This means discount and allowance adjustments need to be provided for each discount reassessed. Notifications enable service providers to track spending across multiple thresholds and profiles, such as specific types of usage, specific products, and services or at the aggregated levels of the customer account or corporate hierarchy.
In Singtel perspective in Rating we have Usage preprocessor , Bulk meter , Multimedia , Resale, Usage Outpayment etc.
The Usage Preprocessor processes incoming CDRs (Call Detail Record) coming from various sources (i.e. CSI, Multi-media, Meter reading, etc.) to produce output CDRs in the Arbor/BP ST01 format. The Usage Preprocessor also processes rejected CDRs from the CSI splitter (stage 1 and 2), handle the usage that come later then X number of day.  Finally, the usage preprocessor also processes priced CDRs generated from CSI stage 3 rejections.  The generated usage file will be sent to Arbor/BP for further processing (guiding and rating). The UPP can reformat an incoming CDR of any format into one or more output CDRs in the ST01 format by using the following functionalities:
recognizing the input format based on an input field
moving input fields to corresponding fields in the ST01 format
filling ST01 fields with values, depending the values of certain fields in the input CDR
massaging the content of input fields depending on the value of other input fields and placing the result in an ST01 field
Set the completion status field to 5, if the transaction date of the incoming usage is older than X number of days.
splitting the output CDR into one or more CDRs and modifying the content of the duplicate CDRs based on values in the input or output CDR.
The UPP modules only provide the tools to perform these functionalities. When a functionality needs to be performed, on which input CDRs and with which values is all table driven and therefore depends on how the UPP is configured.
This document only provides a high-level description of what the UPP modules do. 
Bulk Meter processing
In Bulk Meter processing, there are cyclic reading process, DBMR extractor, exchange reading process, Bulk Meter preprocessing and absorption process.
There are new provide and ceased orders raised everyday.
These orders will be extracted in CSN list to Bulk Meter where the first job, DBMR extractor will extract readings from DBMR based on the service numbers and dates.
After this, the next job “exchange reading process” will update bi_prevreading based on the service numbers and their readings. There could be rejections such as a service number cannot be reprovisioned before it is ceased. These rejections will be updated into bi_report and a report will be sent to Billing Ops via another job.
When a service number is provided in bi_prevreading, it will be billed every week. This happens when the cyclic dump from switch exchange to CSI is passed down to Pegasus and updates the bi_prevreading. The difference in the reading between the cyclic dump and the provision record in bi_prevreading will be sent to Arbor via usage stream and billed accordingly.
About once in two years, the switch exchanges will be upgrading their switches and readings from old switches need to be billed off before the new switches are used.
The absorption module is built to cater for this purpose.
The absorption sort and validate process will check that each input record in the absorption file is in the correct format and any duplicates in the absorption file will be removed and not processed. The accepted records will then be sorted according to their service numbers. Each service number is expected to have one CMO and CMN record which means the old switch reading and new switch reading records.
The update of readings in bi_prevreading will take place via exchange reading process again.
Special Considerations:
 Guiding cyclic record 
The reading date in the Bulk Meter CDR file to Usage Preprocessor is subtracted by 1 to allow the usage to be guided to the correct customer when an SI transfer takes place on same day as cyclic dump.
For instance, service number 61234567 used by customer A is provisioned on 2 Feb 2003 and ceased on 10 Feb 2003. Customer B takes over the service number on 10 Feb 03. If the cyclic dump happens on 10 Feb, current program logic will set the reading date in the CDR file to 10 Feb as well. However, in Arbor, the end date for Customer A is 10 Feb 03 and Bulk Meter usage with reading date on 10 Feb will be guided to customer B that is provisioned on 10 Feb. This results in under-billing for customer A and over-billing for customer B. (see figure A)
If the reading date becomes 9 Feb 03 after subtraction, it will then be guided to the correct customer which is customer A. However, to maintain bill presentation consistency, the reading date before subtraction will be appended to the annotation of the CDR file. The BIF module will then take this date as the to_date in the bill presentation.
Customer A’s usage			Customer B’s usage
2 Feb						10 Feb
Figure A
For existing usage records without to_date in annotation field, BIF module will still be able to cater for them by checking for to_date in the annotation. If there is no to_date, BIF module will take trans_dt as to_date since there is no subtraction done on trans_dt for  usage records before the change.
GST Processing 
To take care of GST revision from 4% to 5%, there will be a TR (Tariff Revision) and cyclic records splitter where TR records will be sent to TR stream while cyclic records to cyclic stream. The purpose of processing TR records is to bill customers at 4% for usage up to 31 Dec 2003. Usage from 1 Jan 2004 onwards at 5% will then be taken care by processing cyclic records.
These TR records would come in with the date on 1 Jan 2004.  In order to compute the local usage before 2004 as 4%, the processed TR records that sent to usage stream (UPP) will be subtracted one day from the TR date which is 31 Dec 2003.  This is because Arbor will rate any usage record dated 1 Jan 2004 as 5% GST. The TR records will first be processed and bi_prevreading will be updated before continuing with the cyclic records.
In addition, CSI will still send TR record even after 1 Jan 2004 for any backdated provision order. Therefore, we need a TR stream to always cater for GST revision for these cases to prevent billing errors. Pls note that before any revision taking place such as on 1 Jan 2004, the S04 rejection checking should be switched off to prevent unnecessary rejections. This is because on 1 Jan 2004, both TR and CYC records send down to Pegasus will have the same date. Hence, it will result S04 rejection when come to CYC record processing after TR record processing.
Besides, E02 checking should be turned on just before 1 Jan 2004 to ensure all the expected TR records are found in the cyclic dump from CSI.
Both S04 and E02 checking can be controlled by setting them in the ini files of TR and cyclic processing jobs.
 Manual Upload
Sometimes, daily orders could have failed during exchange reading process due to no readings found for service numbers or numbers not being assigned in DBMR. This will usually cause the next order to be rejected.
For example, a FIN order is being rejected as W01 due to FIN reading not found for the service number. This service number is then added to the delay file and the search for the FIN reading would continue until the next day. However, if the next provision order comes in the following day, it will be rejected as E04 since the service number is not ceased yet. 
Billing Ops will then need to manual upload the provide record into bi_prevreading. Currently, the manual upload job only allows upload of INI and FIN records to bi_prevreading and a Bulk Meter cdr file will be sent to usage stream at the end of upload process. 
However, we must allow flexibility to upload CYC records into bi_prevreading as well as to have the option whether to send Bulk Meter cdr record to usage stream. At times, OP/OM team could have patched records in OP_CSN that are not extracted to bi_prevreading and we need to patch bi_prevreading accordingly. A more convenient and efficient approach is to allow flexibility of manual upload process to patch records in bi_prevreading without sending down any cdr record to usage for billing.
E02 Check
With five streams of processing jobs, the E02 check which is in processing job BIUBMC201W last time has to be in the new job BIUBMM201W.  This is because each processing stream has only a portion of the full dump and E02 check if carried here, will result in false E02 rejections. E02 check here refers to checking for any missing weekly records for any active number in bi_prevreading.
The new job BIUBMM201W after completion of the 5 streams run, will check for any records in bi_prevreading where proc_flag = N and reading type != FIN. This indicates a situation where weekly record did not come for an active number in bi_prevreading. After completion of BIUBMM201W, a control report will be sent to Actuate to reach Billing Ops for investigation.
Spare lines Recovery
Upon receiving the recovery file, BIURBM201O will need to check whether any of service lines with the Recovery Range is of Spare Status in bi_prevreading and OP_CSN during the Recovery date.
For records under Spare status, they will be archived and removed from bi_prevreading. As for records under Active status, they will be rejected, and records are inserted in bi_report under error code E09 for Billing Ops investigations.
Multimedia billing integration process
SingNet and Magix will be sending prerated charges to Pegasus for convergent billing. The charges will be sent to Pegasus in 3 files, 2 from SingNet and 1 from Magix. The first SingNet file contains itemized usage charges, the second contains RCs, NRCs, adjustments, summarized usage, unit credits and rebates. The Magix file only contains summarized usage. The purpose of the Multimedia billing integration process is to:
Validate the individual files and their content according to the validation rules.
Split the validated records into 2 groups depending on whether they should be uploaded via the usage preprocessor or via the NRC upload program.
Split the NRC upload records into 4 files depending on whether they are account or service instance level NRCs and depending on which customer server (1 or 2) the charges should be guided is to.
Reformat and modify the record to simplify the preprocessor configuration and the NRC upload program.
Produce an error file containing the erroneous records with an error description appended to each record.
Upload the charges through the preprocessor or through the NRC upload program.
Resale
With the launch of Pegasus Phase 2 and the migration of consumer customer data over into Pegasus, the full billing capabilities present in CSI will need to be emulated in Pegasus so as to allow a seamless transition for our customers from the old system to the new.
One such capability will be the handling of Resale Usage currently undertaken solely by CSI. Resale Usage means usage records that are received by SingTel Billing System but are not meant to be billed by SingTel to the end customers who had utilized that service. These usage records will instead be passed to the respective resale customers with SingTel taking a commission off of these resale usages.
The resale dumper module will extract the rated CDRs for the resale dummy service instances in CDR_DATA having external_id like ‘Resale Usage for xx’ and external_id_type is ‘10’ daily based on the rate_dt. The program will then copy these CDRs from CDR_DATA into BI_RESALE_CDR. 
After the CDRs have been copied into BI_RESALE_CDR, each of these CDRs will have its no_bill set to ‘1’ and cdr_status set back to ‘2’,‘3’ or ‘5’. This is done so that the records will not get picked up for billing accidentally or get extracted again into BI_RESALE_CDR in subsequent resale dumper runs.
There will be another 2 programs created for the purpose of extracting Resale usage to the External Operators and producing the reports required to mimic the current workflow in CSI. 
The requirement for the Resale usage extraction is to minimize impact to the External Operators by following existing file formats and reports as closely as possible.
The pre-extraction module will calculate and populate records in BI_RESALE_CDR with the information to be extracted by the Resale extraction module. The extraction module will then extract CDRs belonging to the relevant External operator from BI_RESALE_CDR into an output file and produce some reports to be sent together to the External Operator.
The usg_extract date field in BI_RESALE_CDR will be populated with the system date during the extraction job run when the CDRs are extracted and sent to the External Operators based on the agreed frequency. This is to prevent duplicate extractions.
For extractions that are weekly (currently StarHub), a monthly job will be scheduled on the 1st of the next month to extract all resale usage for that operator, which had not been extracted before, from the last weekly extraction to the end of the month.
Resale Traffic Types for extraction will include: 01, 06, 14, 15, 16 and 31.
BFDD’s for Resale usages.
Outpayment usage.
Calls made using the subscriber’s personal credit card via the Operator Assisted, or Manual Trunk Call – need to be extracted on weekly basis to UOB Bank and On-Demand system. This is needed in order for the bank, which is the clearing house for such transactions to pay Singtel weekly through the Giro system. The reports generated for the On Demand System is needed in order to enable customer’s queries on their credit card calls to be handled. Hard copy reports are also generated for Billing Operations for consolidation purposes.

Thresholding
Amdocs Kenan includes controls in the rating process. It is important to note that the time which is critical for some of the controls is dependent on the mediation solution that sends the EDRs to Amdocs Kenan.  
In response to the need for ever-tighter control of financial risk, Amdocs Kenan offers a “fast batch” rating process flow which converts unrated files from mediation to rated and accumulated events in the billing database. Within this flow, the charge accumulator provides the scope for a variety of types of intervention with the service end-user, though is primarily intended for enterprise customers who do not necessarily require split-second response times when unbilled spending thresholds are breached.
Advanced Rating – Thresholding module is a powerful solution for telecommunications operators, especially those with mobile and internet services, who require near real-time accumulation of usage charges for comparison against configurable threshold parameters. This module monitors any network usage against flexible parameters and offers multiple channels for acting when a threshold has been exceeded. Thresholding maximizes return on investment by ensuring end-users stay within the set usage boundaries, and it manages fraud risk by initiating actions whenever a customer's eligible outstanding usage exceeds predefined amounts. In addition, thresholding can be used to increase customer satisfaction and retention by triggering events that reward customers for their usage.  
Advanced Rating – Thresholding module keeps a running total of usage events for the billing product accounts and account components. Accumulation of usage data can be performed for any product of any service instance and for all accounts in any associated account hierarchy.
Accumulation provides an estimate of the unbilled usage charges within a hierarchy, account, service instance, product or usage type. The running totals are kept for rated amounts and for usage units. Totals can provide a picture of usage by account, service instance or product in an event-driven manner. This information is always available and can be used in conjunction with external systems, such as Interactive Voice Recognition (IVR), to provide up-to-date information to existing customers, thus decreasing incoming call volumes (This may require integration with specific IVR systems). By using provisioned threshold profiles, running totals can be used to initiate actions in various ways. 
Figure 25	Thresholding Actions
The Advanced Rating – Thresholding module tracks totals of usage, recurring charges, non-recurring charges and unit credits. For instance, operators can use alarms to notify customers who have exceeded threshold limits, to warn supervisors of fraud risks or to reward customers for their usage. It is possible to set multiple alarms, as well as act throughout the account hierarchy. These actions can also trigger the execution of a script and/or actions can be triggered in provisioning systems. For example, the operator could automatically terminate service for fraudulent or credit-risk customers (a provisioning system-specific integration would need to be in place for this action to be fully automated).
