2. BUSINESS OVERVIEW AND FUNCTIONA.2.1. Kenan:
The agreed solution is based on the following high-level principles.
As baseline, provide front-end users with familiar experiences including similar processes and screens with an up-dated look-and-feel
Update technology stack to build screens and integration layer
Modernize hardware and third-party software
Consolidate commercial catalog, rules engine and improve product configuration capabilities
Minimize impact on external applications by uplifting the existing enterprise application integration solution with like-for-like services
Leverage Release 1, bridging solution as the end-state routing layer, where required, between Group Consumer and Group Enterprise-specific applications
Minimize impact on the Release 1 solution – avoid tightly coupled interfaces
Enable order flow-through from external order capture channels to BCC and on to provisioning
Figure 1 As-Is and To-Be Application Landscape
Figure 2 Target Functional Architecture

3. Kenan System Overview.Kenan Module List:
Billing
Singtel Billing includes the 26 Bill cycles in a month starting from 1st (Billing execution starts from 3rd of the month)  from every month to 26th/27th of the Month. We have 3 types of billing in Singtel in a day.
Cyclic Billing 
This is scheduled Bill cycles for the day like M01, C01, R01 etc. 
Non-Cyclic Billing 
Non-Cycle Billing includes the interim bills and fallout/catch up cases for previous Bill cycles.
Proforma Billing
Proforma Billing is to validate some test bills  before the final bill cycle.
Bill Processing
Bill processing comprises of stream of jobs. However, this document only focuses on four jobs:
BIP Initialization
Script for BIP Execution
Post BIP Error Detection Script
Script to dump BBCQ and BIU – before bill run
Script to dump BBCQ and BIU – after bill run
These four jobs are part of the Bill Cycle (Cyclic and Non-cyclic) Processing Stream. The flow is illustrated below:
The other jobs in the Bill Cycle Processing Stream will not be documented here. However, this document will address the guideline/standard of designing jobs to be run in the Bill Cycle Processing Stream. 
For more details on Billing. Please refer the BFDD document as below.  Latest JPS also attached for reference.
Rating
Amdocs Kenan supports file-based offline rating for post-paid subscribers. The rating engine supports a sophisticated model based on customer and product offering characteristics as well as admitting in-line promotions and charge monitoring for notification purposes. The engine delivers high performance and supports diverse interpretations of chargeable events. 
The Message Processing System (MPS) calculates usage charges for customers (and in some cases for foreign accounts as well). MPS performs the following tasks
Batch Usage Processing Flow
Collects usage files from a network mediation layer.
Parses each file to determine the type, time, duration, and other properties of corresponding usage events. 
Guides each usage event to an Amdocs Kenan or external account. 
Rates each usage event and stores the usage charge and related information in the database.
Exports out collects (rated usage events for foreign carriers) and reseller usage events.
Usage can be rated based on duration, volume, location, time of day, jurisdiction, zone class, distance band, bill class, provide class, type of product, equipment class code, service code and many more attributes and combinations. It’s possible to have inputs in one unit and rating in different units. For each charge, minimum and per unit charges can be also defined. Amdocs Kenan also supports pre-rated usage to be re-rated or loaded without applying additional charges.
In normal invoice processing, discounts and allowance are applied on usage collected during the current bill run, regardless if it’s late or not. In such a case, a late call from a previous month will consume allowance of the current month. Amdocs Kenan also supports special late usage handling through configuration which allows late usage needs to be discounted based on the month it belongs to (event transaction date) and re-calculate related discounts applied to previous invoices. This means discount and allowance adjustments need to be provided for each discount reassessed. Notifications enable service providers to track spending across multiple thresholds and profiles, such as specific types of usage, specific products, and services or at the aggregated levels of the customer account or corporate hierarchy.
In Singtel perspective in Rating we have Usage preprocessor , Bulk meter , Multimedia , Resale, Usage Outpayment etc.
The Usage Preprocessor processes incoming CDRs (Call Detail Record) coming from various sources (i.e. CSI, Multi-media, Meter reading, etc.) to produce output CDRs in the Arbor/BP ST01 format. The Usage Preprocessor also processes rejected CDRs from the CSI splitter (stage 1 and 2), handle the usage that come later then X number of day.  Finally, the usage preprocessor also processes priced CDRs generated from CSI stage 3 rejections.  The generated usage file will be sent to Arbor/BP for further processing (guiding and rating). The UPP can reformat an incoming CDR of any format into one or more output CDRs in the ST01 format by using the following functionalities:
recognizing the input format based on an input field
moving input fields to corresponding fields in the ST01 format
filling ST01 fields with values, depending the values of certain fields in the input CDR
massaging the content of input fields depending on the value of other input fields and placing the result in an ST01 field
Set the completion status field to 5, if the transaction date of the incoming usage is older than X number of days.
splitting the output CDR into one or more CDRs and modifying the content of the duplicate CDRs based on values in the input or output CDR.
The UPP modules only provide the tools to perform these functionalities. When a functionality needs to be performed, on which input CDRs and with which values is all table driven and therefore depends on how the UPP is configured.
This document only provides a high-level description of what the UPP modules do. 
Bulk Meter processing
In Bulk Meter processing, there are cyclic reading process, DBMR extractor, exchange reading process, Bulk Meter preprocessing and absorption process.
There are new provide and ceased orders raised everyday.
These orders will be extracted in CSN list to Bulk Meter where the first job, DBMR extractor will extract readings from DBMR based on the service numbers and dates.
After this, the next job “exchange reading process” will update bi_prevreading based on the service numbers and their readings. There could be rejections such as a service number cannot be reprovisioned before it is ceased. These rejections will be updated into bi_report and a report will be sent to Billing Ops via another job.
When a service number is provided in bi_prevreading, it will be billed every week. This happens when the cyclic dump from switch exchange to CSI is passed down to Pegasus and updates the bi_prevreading. The difference in the reading between the cyclic dump and the provision record in bi_prevreading will be sent to Arbor via usage stream and billed accordingly.
About once in two years, the switch exchanges will be upgrading their switches and readings from old switches need to be billed off before the new switches are used.
The absorption module is built to cater for this purpose.
The absorption sort and validate process will check that each input record in the absorption file is in the correct format and any duplicates in the absorption file will be removed and not processed. The accepted records will then be sorted according to their service numbers. Each service number is expected to have one CMO and CMN record which means the old switch reading and new switch reading records.
The update of readings in bi_prevreading will take place via exchange reading process again.
Special Considerations:
 Guiding cyclic record 
The reading date in the Bulk Meter CDR file to Usage Preprocessor is subtracted by 1 to allow the usage to be guided to the correct customer when an SI transfer takes place on same day as cyclic dump.
For instance, service number 61234567 used by customer A is provisioned on 2 Feb 2003 and ceased on 10 Feb 2003. Customer B takes over the service number on 10 Feb 03. If the cyclic dump happens on 10 Feb, current program logic will set the reading date in the CDR file to 10 Feb as well. However, in Arbor, the end date for Customer A is 10 Feb 03 and Bulk Meter usage with reading date on 10 Feb will be guided to customer B that is provisioned on 10 Feb. This results in under-billing for customer A and over-billing for customer B. (see figure A)
If the reading date becomes 9 Feb 03 after subtraction, it will then be guided to the correct customer which is customer A. However, to maintain bill presentation consistency, the reading date before subtraction will be appended to the annotation of the CDR file. The BIF module will then take this date as the to_date in the bill presentation.
Customer A’s usage			Customer B’s usage
2 Feb						10 Feb
Figure A
For existing usage records without to_date in annotation field, BIF module will still be able to cater for them by checking for to_date in the annotation. If there is no to_date, BIF module will take trans_dt as to_date since there is no subtraction done on trans_dt for  usage records before the change.
GST Processing 
To take care of GST revision from 4% to 5%, there will be a TR (Tariff Revision) and cyclic records splitter where TR records will be sent to TR stream while cyclic records to cyclic stream. The purpose of processing TR records is to bill customers at 4% for usage up to 31 Dec 2003. Usage from 1 Jan 2004 onwards at 5% will then be taken care by processing cyclic records.
These TR records would come in with the date on 1 Jan 2004.  In order to compute the local usage before 2004 as 4%, the processed TR records that sent to usage stream (UPP) will be subtracted one day from the TR date which is 31 Dec 2003.  This is because Arbor will rate any usage record dated 1 Jan 2004 as 5% GST. The TR records will first be processed and bi_prevreading will be updated before continuing with the cyclic records.
In addition, CSI will still send TR record even after 1 Jan 2004 for any backdated provision order. Therefore, we need a TR stream to always cater for GST revision for these cases to prevent billing errors. Pls note that before any revision taking place such as on 1 Jan 2004, the S04 rejection checking should be switched off to prevent unnecessary rejections. This is because on 1 Jan 2004, both TR and CYC records send down to Pegasus will have the same date. Hence, it will result S04 rejection when come to CYC record processing after TR record processing.
Besides, E02 checking should be turned on just before 1 Jan 2004 to ensure all the expected TR records are found in the cyclic dump from CSI.
Both S04 and E02 checking can be controlled by setting them in the ini files of TR and cyclic processing jobs.
 Manual Upload
Sometimes, daily orders could have failed during exchange reading process due to no readings found for service numbers or numbers not being assigned in DBMR. This will usually cause the next order to be rejected.
For example, a FIN order is being rejected as W01 due to FIN reading not found for the service number. This service number is then added to the delay file and the search for the FIN reading would continue until the next day. However, if the next provision order comes in the following day, it will be rejected as E04 since the service number is not ceased yet. 
Billing Ops will then need to manual upload the provide record into bi_prevreading. Currently, the manual upload job only allows upload of INI and FIN records to bi_prevreading and a Bulk Meter cdr file will be sent to usage stream at the end of upload process. 
However, we must allow flexibility to upload CYC records into bi_prevreading as well as to have the option whether to send Bulk Meter cdr record to usage stream. At times, OP/OM team could have patched records in OP_CSN that are not extracted to bi_prevreading and we need to patch bi_prevreading accordingly. A more convenient and efficient approach is to allow flexibility of manual upload process to patch records in bi_prevreading without sending down any cdr record to usage for billing.
E02 Check
With five streams of processing jobs, the E02 check which is in processing job BIUBMC201W last time has to be in the new job BIUBMM201W.  This is because each processing stream has only a portion of the full dump and E02 check if carried here, will result in false E02 rejections. E02 check here refers to checking for any missing weekly records for any active number in bi_prevreading.
The new job BIUBMM201W after completion of the 5 streams run, will check for any records in bi_prevreading where proc_flag = N and reading type != FIN. This indicates a situation where weekly record did not come for an active number in bi_prevreading. After completion of BIUBMM201W, a control report will be sent to Actuate to reach Billing Ops for investigation.
Spare lines Recovery
Upon receiving the recovery file, BIURBM201O will need to check whether any of service lines with the Recovery Range is of Spare Status in bi_prevreading and OP_CSN during the Recovery date.
For records under Spare status, they will be archived and removed from bi_prevreading. As for records under Active status, they will be rejected, and records are inserted in bi_report under error code E09 for Billing Ops investigations.
Multimedia billing integration process
SingNet and Magix will be sending prerated charges to Pegasus for convergent billing. The charges will be sent to Pegasus in 3 files, 2 from SingNet and 1 from Magix. The first SingNet file contains itemized usage charges, the second contains RCs, NRCs, adjustments, summarized usage, unit credits and rebates. The Magix file only contains summarized usage. The purpose of the Multimedia billing integration process is to:
Validate the individual files and their content according to the validation rules.
Split the validated records into 2 groups depending on whether they should be uploaded via the usage preprocessor or via the NRC upload program.
Split the NRC upload records into 4 files depending on whether they are account or service instance level NRCs and depending on which customer server (1 or 2) the charges should be guided is to.
Reformat and modify the record to simplify the preprocessor configuration and the NRC upload program.
Produce an error file containing the erroneous records with an error description appended to each record.
Upload the charges through the preprocessor or through the NRC upload program.
Resale
With the launch of Pegasus Phase 2 and the migration of consumer customer data over into Pegasus, the full billing capabilities present in CSI will need to be emulated in Pegasus so as to allow a seamless transition for our customers from the old system to the new.
One such capability will be the handling of Resale Usage currently undertaken solely by CSI. Resale Usage means usage records that are received by SingTel Billing System but are not meant to be billed by SingTel to the end customers who had utilized that service. These usage records will instead be passed to the respective resale customers with SingTel taking a commission off of these resale usages.
The resale dumper module will extract the rated CDRs for the resale dummy service instances in CDR_DATA having external_id like ‘Resale Usage for xx’ and external_id_type is ‘10’ daily based on the rate_dt. The program will then copy these CDRs from CDR_DATA into BI_RESALE_CDR. 
After the CDRs have been copied into BI_RESALE_CDR, each of these CDRs will have its no_bill set to ‘1’ and cdr_status set back to ‘2’,‘3’ or ‘5’. This is done so that the records will not get picked up for billing accidentally or get extracted again into BI_RESALE_CDR in subsequent resale dumper runs.
There will be another 2 programs created for the purpose of extracting Resale usage to the External Operators and producing the reports required to mimic the current workflow in CSI. 
The requirement for the Resale usage extraction is to minimize impact to the External Operators by following existing file formats and reports as closely as possible.
The pre-extraction module will calculate and populate records in BI_RESALE_CDR with the information to be extracted by the Resale extraction module. The extraction module will then extract CDRs belonging to the relevant External operator from BI_RESALE_CDR into an output file and produce some reports to be sent together to the External Operator.
The usg_extract date field in BI_RESALE_CDR will be populated with the system date during the extraction job run when the CDRs are extracted and sent to the External Operators based on the agreed frequency. This is to prevent duplicate extractions.
For extractions that are weekly (currently StarHub), a monthly job will be scheduled on the 1st of the next month to extract all resale usage for that operator, which had not been extracted before, from the last weekly extraction to the end of the month.
Resale Traffic Types for extraction will include: 01, 06, 14, 15, 16 and 31.
BFDD’s for Resale usages.
Outpayment usage.
Calls made using the subscriber’s personal credit card via the Operator Assisted, or Manual Trunk Call – need to be extracted on weekly basis to UOB Bank and On-Demand system. This is needed in order for the bank, which is the clearing house for such transactions to pay Singtel weekly through the Giro system. The reports generated for the On Demand System is needed in order to enable customer’s queries on their credit card calls to be handled. Hard copy reports are also generated for Billing Operations for consolidation purposes.

Thresholding
Amdocs Kenan includes controls in the rating process. It is important to note that the time which is critical for some of the controls is dependent on the mediation solution that sends the EDRs to Amdocs Kenan.  
In response to the need for ever-tighter control of financial risk, Amdocs Kenan offers a “fast batch” rating process flow which converts unrated files from mediation to rated and accumulated events in the billing database. Within this flow, the charge accumulator provides the scope for a variety of types of intervention with the service end-user, though is primarily intended for enterprise customers who do not necessarily require split-second response times when unbilled spending thresholds are breached.
Advanced Rating – Thresholding module is a powerful solution for telecommunications operators, especially those with mobile and internet services, who require near real-time accumulation of usage charges for comparison against configurable threshold parameters. This module monitors any network usage against flexible parameters and offers multiple channels for acting when a threshold has been exceeded. Thresholding maximizes return on investment by ensuring end-users stay within the set usage boundaries, and it manages fraud risk by initiating actions whenever a customer's eligible outstanding usage exceeds predefined amounts. In addition, thresholding can be used to increase customer satisfaction and retention by triggering events that reward customers for their usage.  
Advanced Rating – Thresholding module keeps a running total of usage events for the billing product accounts and account components. Accumulation of usage data can be performed for any product of any service instance and for all accounts in any associated account hierarchy.
Accumulation provides an estimate of the unbilled usage charges within a hierarchy, account, service instance, product or usage type. The running totals are kept for rated amounts and for usage units. Totals can provide a picture of usage by account, service instance or product in an event-driven manner. This information is always available and can be used in conjunction with external systems, such as Interactive Voice Recognition (IVR), to provide up-to-date information to existing customers, thus decreasing incoming call volumes (This may require integration with specific IVR systems). By using provisioned threshold profiles, running totals can be used to initiate actions in various ways. 
Figure 25	Thresholding Actions
The Advanced Rating – Thresholding module tracks totals of usage, recurring charges, non-recurring charges and unit credits. For instance, operators can use alarms to notify customers who have exceeded threshold limits, to warn supervisors of fraud risks or to reward customers for their usage. It is possible to set multiple alarms, as well as act throughout the account hierarchy. These actions can also trigger the execution of a script and/or actions can be triggered in provisioning systems. For example, the operator could automatically terminate service for fraudulent or credit-risk customers (a provisioning system-specific integration would need to be in place for this action to be fully automated).

    "Kenan Module List": "Billing
Singtel Billing includes the 26 Bill cycles in a month starting from 1st (Billing execution starts from 3rd of the month)  from every month to 26th/27th of the Month. We have 3 types of billing in Singtel in a day.
Cyclic Billing 
This is scheduled Bill cycles for the day like M01, C01, R01 etc. 
Non-Cyclic Billing 
Non-Cycle Billing includes the interim bills and fallout/catch up cases for previous Bill cycles.
Proforma Billing
Proforma Billing is to validate some test bills  before the final bill cycle.
Bill Processing
Bill processing comprises of stream of jobs. However, this document only focuses on four jobs:
BIP Initialization
Script for BIP Execution
Post BIP Error Detection Script
Script to dump BBCQ and BIU – before bill run
Script to dump BBCQ and BIU – after bill run
These four jobs are part of the Bill Cycle (Cyclic and Non-cyclic) Processing Stream. The flow is illustrated below:
The other jobs in the Bill Cycle Processing Stream will not be documented here. However, this document will address the guideline/standard of designing jobs to be run in the Bill Cycle Processing Stream. 
For more details on Billing. Please refer the BFDD document as below.  Latest JPS also attached for reference.
Rating
Amdocs Kenan supports file-based offline rating for post-paid subscribers. The rating engine supports a sophisticated model based on customer and product offering characteristics as well as admitting in-line promotions and charge monitoring for notification purposes. The engine delivers high performance and supports diverse interpretations of chargeable events. 
The Message Processing System (MPS) calculates usage charges for customers (and in some cases for foreign accounts as well). MPS performs the following tasks
Batch Usage Processing Flow
Collects usage files from a network mediation layer.
Parses each file to determine the type, time, duration, and other properties of corresponding usage events. 
Guides each usage event to an Amdocs Kenan or external account. 
Rates each usage event and stores the usage charge and related information in the database.
Exports out collects (rated usage events for foreign carriers) and reseller usage events.
Usage can be rated based on duration, volume, location, time of day, jurisdiction, zone class, distance band, bill class, provide class, type of product, equipment class code, service code and many more attributes and combinations. It’s possible to have inputs in one unit and rating in different units. For each charge, minimum and per unit charges can be also defined. Amdocs Kenan also supports pre-rated usage to be re-rated or loaded without applying additional charges.
In normal invoice processing, discounts and allowance are applied on usage collected during the current bill run, regardless if it’s late or not. In such a case, a late call from a previous month will consume allowance of the current month. Amdocs Kenan also supports special late usage handling through configuration which allows late usage needs to be discounted based on the month it belongs to (event transaction date) and re-calculate related discounts applied to previous invoices. This means discount and allowance adjustments need to be provided for each discount reassessed. Notifications enable service providers to track spending across multiple thresholds and profiles, such as specific types of usage, specific products, and services or at the aggregated levels of the customer account or corporate hierarchy.
In Singtel perspective in Rating we have Usage preprocessor , Bulk meter , Multimedia , Resale, Usage Outpayment etc.
The Usage Preprocessor processes incoming CDRs (Call Detail Record) coming from various sources (i.e. CSI, Multi-media, Meter reading, etc.) to produce output CDRs in the Arbor/BP ST01 format. The Usage Preprocessor also processes rejected CDRs from the CSI splitter (stage 1 and 2), handle the usage that come later then X number of day.  Finally, the usage preprocessor also processes priced CDRs generated from CSI stage 3 rejections.  The generated usage file will be sent to Arbor/BP for further processing (guiding and rating). The UPP can reformat an incoming CDR of any format into one or more output CDRs in the ST01 format by using the following functionalities:
recognizing the input format based on an input field
moving input fields to corresponding fields in the ST01 format
filling ST01 fields with values, depending the values of certain fields in the input CDR
massaging the content of input fields depending on the value of other input fields and placing the result in an ST01 field
Set the completion status field to 5, if the transaction date of the incoming usage is older than X number of days.
splitting the output CDR into one or more CDRs and modifying the content of the duplicate CDRs based on values in the input or output CDR.
The UPP modules only provide the tools to perform these functionalities. When a functionality needs to be performed, on which input CDRs and with which values is all table driven and therefore depends on how the UPP is configured.
This document only provides a high-level description of what the UPP modules do. 
Bulk Meter processing
In Bulk Meter processing, there are cyclic reading process, DBMR extractor, exchange reading process, Bulk Meter preprocessing and absorption process.
There are new provide and ceased orders raised everyday.
These orders will be extracted in CSN list to Bulk Meter where the first job, DBMR extractor will extract readings from DBMR based on the service numbers and dates.
After this, the next job “exchange reading process” will update bi_prevreading based on the service numbers and their readings. There could be rejections such as a service number cannot be reprovisioned before it is ceased. These rejections will be updated into bi_report and a report will be sent to Billing Ops via another job.
When a service number is provided in bi_prevreading, it will be billed every week. This happens when the cyclic dump from switch exchange to CSI is passed down to Pegasus and updates the bi_prevreading. The difference in the reading between the cyclic dump and the provision record in bi_prevreading will be sent to Arbor via usage stream and billed accordingly.
About once in two years, the switch exchanges will be upgrading their switches and readings from old switches need to be billed off before the new switches are used.
The absorption module is built to cater for this purpose.
The absorption sort and validate process will check that each input record in the absorption file is in the correct format and any duplicates in the absorption file will be removed and not processed. The accepted records will then be sorted according to their service numbers. Each service number is expected to have one CMO and CMN record which means the old switch reading and new switch reading records.
The update of readings in bi_prevreading will take place via exchange reading process again.
Special Considerations:
 Guiding cyclic record 
The reading date in the Bulk Meter CDR file to Usage Preprocessor is subtracted by 1 to allow the usage to be guided to the correct customer when an SI transfer takes place on same day as cyclic dump.
For instance, service number 61234567 used by customer A is provisioned on 2 Feb 2003 and ceased on 10 Feb 2003. Customer B takes over the service number on 10 Feb 03. If the cyclic dump happens on 10 Feb, current program logic will set the reading date in the CDR file to 10 Feb as well. However, in Arbor, the end date for Customer A is 10 Feb 03 and Bulk Meter usage with reading date on 10 Feb will be guided to customer B that is provisioned on 10 Feb. This results in under-billing for customer A and over-billing for customer B. (see figure A)
If the reading date becomes 9 Feb 03 after subtraction, it will then be guided to the correct customer which is customer A. However, to maintain bill presentation consistency, the reading date before subtraction will be appended to the annotation of the CDR file. The BIF module will then take this date as the to_date in the bill presentation.

For existing usage records without to_date in annotation field, BIF module will still be able to cater for them by checking for to_date in the annotation. If there is no to_date, BIF module will take trans_dt as to_date since there is no subtraction done on trans_dt for  usage records before the change.
GST Processing 
To take care of GST revision from 4% to 5%, there will be a TR (Tariff Revision) and cyclic records splitter where TR records will be sent to TR stream while cyclic records to cyclic stream. The purpose of processing TR records is to bill customers at 4% for usage up to 31 Dec 2003. Usage from 1 Jan 2004 onwards at 5% will then be taken care by processing cyclic records.
These TR records would come in with the date on 1 Jan 2004.  In order to compute the local usage before 2004 as 4%, the processed TR records that sent to usage stream (UPP) will be subtracted one day from the TR date which is 31 Dec 2003.  This is because Arbor will rate any usage record dated 1 Jan 2004 as 5% GST. The TR records will first be processed and bi_prevreading will be updated before continuing with the cyclic records.
In addition, CSI will still send TR record even after 1 Jan 2004 for any backdated provision order. Therefore, we need a TR stream to always cater for GST revision for these cases to prevent billing errors. Pls note that before any revision taking place such as on 1 Jan 2004, the S04 rejection checking should be switched off to prevent unnecessary rejections. This is because on 1 Jan 2004, both TR and CYC records send down to Pegasus will have the same date. Hence, it will result S04 rejection when come to CYC record processing after TR record processing.
Besides, E02 checking should be turned on just before 1 Jan 2004 to ensure all the expected TR records are found in the cyclic dump from CSI.
Both S04 and E02 checking can be controlled by setting them in the ini files of TR and cyclic processing jobs.
 Manual Upload
Sometimes, daily orders could have failed during exchange reading process due to no readings found for service numbers or numbers not being assigned in DBMR. This will usually cause the next order to be rejected.
For example, a FIN order is being rejected as W01 due to FIN reading not found for the service number. This service number is then added to the delay file and the search for the FIN reading would continue until the next day. However, if the next provision order comes in the following day, it will be rejected as E04 since the service number is not ceased yet. 
Billing Ops will then need to manual upload the provide record into bi_prevreading. Currently, the manual upload job only allows upload of INI and FIN records to bi_prevreading and a Bulk Meter cdr file will be sent to usage stream at the end of upload process. 
However, we must allow flexibility to upload CYC records into bi_prevreading as well as to have the option whether to send Bulk Meter cdr record to usage stream. At times, OP/OM team could have patched records in OP_CSN that are not extracted to bi_prevreading and we need to patch bi_prevreading accordingly. A more convenient and efficient approach is to allow flexibility of manual upload process to patch records in bi_prevreading without sending down any cdr record to usage for billing.
E02 Check
With five streams of processing jobs, the E02 check which is in processing job BIUBMC201W last time has to be in the new job BIUBMM201W.  This is because each processing stream has only a portion of the full dump and E02 check if carried here, will result in false E02 rejections. E02 check here refers to checking for any missing weekly records for any active number in bi_prevreading.
The new job BIUBMM201W after completion of the 5 streams run, will check for any records in bi_prevreading where proc_flag = N and reading type != FIN. This indicates a situation where weekly record did not come for an active number in bi_prevreading. After completion of BIUBMM201W, a control report will be sent to Actuate to reach Billing Ops for investigation.
Spare lines Recovery
Upon receiving the recovery file, BIURBM201O will need to check whether any of service lines with the Recovery Range is of Spare Status in bi_prevreading and OP_CSN during the Recovery date.
For records under Spare status, they will be archived and removed from bi_prevreading. As for records under Active status, they will be rejected, and records are inserted in bi_report under error code E09 for Billing Ops investigations.
Multimedia billing integration process
SingNet and Magix will be sending prerated charges to Pegasus for convergent billing. The charges will be sent to Pegasus in 3 files, 2 from SingNet and 1 from Magix. The first SingNet file contains itemized usage charges, the second contains RCs, NRCs, adjustments, summarized usage, unit credits and rebates. The Magix file only contains summarized usage. The purpose of the Multimedia billing integration process is to:
Validate the individual files and their content according to the validation rules.
Split the validated records into 2 groups depending on whether they should be uploaded via the usage preprocessor or via the NRC upload program.
Split the NRC upload records into 4 files depending on whether they are account or service instance level NRCs and depending on which customer server (1 or 2) the charges should be guided is to.
Reformat and modify the record to simplify the preprocessor configuration and the NRC upload program.
Produce an error file containing the erroneous records with an error description appended to each record.
Upload the charges through the preprocessor or through the NRC upload program.
Resale
With the launch of Pegasus Phase 2 and the migration of consumer customer data over into Pegasus, the full billing capabilities present in CSI will need to be emulated in Pegasus so as to allow a seamless transition for our customers from the old system to the new.
One such capability will be the handling of Resale Usage currently undertaken solely by CSI. Resale Usage means usage records that are received by SingTel Billing System but are not meant to be billed by SingTel to the end customers who had utilized that service. These usage records will instead be passed to the respective resale customers with SingTel taking a commission off of these resale usages.
The resale dumper module will extract the rated CDRs for the resale dummy service instances in CDR_DATA having external_id like ‘Resale Usage for xx’ and external_id_type is ‘10’ daily based on the rate_dt. The program will then copy these CDRs from CDR_DATA into BI_RESALE_CDR. 
After the CDRs have been copied into BI_RESALE_CDR, each of these CDRs will have its no_bill set to ‘1’ and cdr_status set back to ‘2’,‘3’ or ‘5’. This is done so that the records will not get picked up for billing accidentally or get extracted again into BI_RESALE_CDR in subsequent resale dumper runs.
There will be another 2 programs created for the purpose of extracting Resale usage to the External Operators and producing the reports required to mimic the current workflow in CSI. 
The requirement for the Resale usage extraction is to minimize impact to the External Operators by following existing file formats and reports as closely as possible.
The pre-extraction module will calculate and populate records in BI_RESALE_CDR with the information to be extracted by the Resale extraction module. The extraction module will then extract CDRs belonging to the relevant External operator from BI_RESALE_CDR into an output file and produce some reports to be sent together to the External Operator.
The usg_extract date field in BI_RESALE_CDR will be populated with the system date during the extraction job run when the CDRs are extracted and sent to the External Operators based on the agreed frequency. This is to prevent duplicate extractions.
For extractions that are weekly (currently StarHub), a monthly job will be scheduled on the 1st of the next month to extract all resale usage for that operator, which had not been extracted before, from the last weekly extraction to the end of the month.
Resale Traffic Types for extraction will include: 01, 06, 14, 15, 16 and 31.

Thresholding
Amdocs Kenan includes controls in the rating process. It is important to note that the time which is critical for some of the controls is dependent on the mediation solution that sends the EDRs to Amdocs Kenan.  
In response to the need for ever-tighter control of financial risk, Amdocs Kenan offers a “fast batch” rating process flow which converts unrated files from mediation to rated and accumulated events in the billing database. Within this flow, the charge accumulator provides the scope for a variety of types of intervention with the service end-user, though is primarily intended for enterprise customers who do not necessarily require split-second response times when unbilled spending thresholds are breached.
Advanced Rating – Thresholding module is a powerful solution for telecommunications operators, especially those with mobile and internet services, who require near real-time accumulation of usage charges for comparison against configurable threshold parameters. This module monitors any network usage against flexible parameters and offers multiple channels for acting when a threshold has been exceeded. Thresholding maximizes return on investment by ensuring end-users stay within the set usage boundaries, and it manages fraud risk by initiating actions whenever a customer's eligible outstanding usage exceeds predefined amounts. In addition, thresholding can be used to increase customer satisfaction and retention by triggering events that reward customers for their usage.  
Advanced Rating – Thresholding module keeps a running total of usage events for the billing product accounts and account components. Accumulation of usage data can be performed for any product of any service instance and for all accounts in any associated account hierarchy.
Accumulation provides an estimate of the unbilled usage charges within a hierarchy, account, service instance, product or usage type. The running totals are kept for rated amounts and for usage units. Totals can provide a picture of usage by account, service instance or product in an event-driven manner. This information is always available and can be used in conjunction with external systems, such as Interactive Voice Recognition (IVR), to provide up-to-date information to existing customers, thus decreasing incoming call volumes (This may require integration with specific IVR systems). By using provisioned threshold profiles, running totals can be used to initiate actions in various ways. 
Figure 25	Thresholding Actions
The Advanced Rating – Thresholding module tracks totals of usage, recurring charges, non-recurring charges and unit credits. For instance, operators can use alarms to notify customers who have exceeded threshold limits, to warn supervisors of fraud risks or to reward customers for their usage. It is possible to set multiple alarms, as well as act throughout the account hierarchy. These actions can also trigger the execution of a script and/or actions can be triggered in provisioning systems. For example, the operator could automatically terminate service for fraudulent or credit-risk customers (a provisioning system-specific integration would need to be in place for this action to be fully automated).

2. BUSINESS OVERVIEW AND FUNCTIONA.2.1. Kenan:
The agreed solution is based on the following high-level principles.
As baseline, provide front-end users with familiar experiences including similar processes and screens with an up-dated look-and-feel
Update technology stack to build screens and integration layer
Modernize hardware and third-party software
Consolidate commercial catalog, rules engine and improve product configuration capabilities
Minimize impact on external applications by uplifting the existing enterprise application integration solution with like-for-like services
Leverage Release 1, bridging solution as the end-state routing layer, where required, between Group Consumer and Group Enterprise-specific applications
Minimize impact on the Release 1 solution – avoid tightly coupled interfaces
Enable order flow-through from external order capture channels to BCC and on to provisioning
Figure 1 As-Is and To-Be Application Landscape
Figure 2 Target Functional Architecture

3. Kenan System Overview.Kenan Module List:
Billing
Singtel Billing includes the 26 Bill cycles in a month starting from 1st (Billing execution starts from 3rd of the month)  from every month to 26th/27th of the Month. We have 3 types of billing in Singtel in a day.
Cyclic Billing 
This is scheduled Bill cycles for the day like M01, C01, R01 etc. 
Non-Cyclic Billing 
Non-Cycle Billing includes the interim bills and fallout/catch up cases for previous Bill cycles.
Proforma Billing
Proforma Billing is to validate some test bills  before the final bill cycle.
Bill Processing
Bill processing comprises of stream of jobs. However, this document only focuses on four jobs:
BIP Initialization
Script for BIP Execution
Post BIP Error Detection Script
Script to dump BBCQ and BIU – before bill run
Script to dump BBCQ and BIU – after bill run
These four jobs are part of the Bill Cycle (Cyclic and Non-cyclic) Processing Stream. The flow is illustrated below:
The other jobs in the Bill Cycle Processing Stream will not be documented here. However, this document will address the guideline/standard of designing jobs to be run in the Bill Cycle Processing Stream. 
For more details on Billing. Please refer the BFDD document as below.  Latest JPS also attached for reference.
Rating
Amdocs Kenan supports file-based offline rating for post-paid subscribers. The rating engine supports a sophisticated model based on customer and product offering characteristics as well as admitting in-line promotions and charge monitoring for notification purposes. The engine delivers high performance and supports diverse interpretations of chargeable events. 
The Message Processing System (MPS) calculates usage charges for customers (and in some cases for foreign accounts as well). MPS performs the following tasks
Batch Usage Processing Flow
Collects usage files from a network mediation layer.
Parses each file to determine the type, time, duration, and other properties of corresponding usage events. 
Guides each usage event to an Amdocs Kenan or external account. 
Rates each usage event and stores the usage charge and related information in the database.
Exports out collects (rated usage events for foreign carriers) and reseller usage events.
Usage can be rated based on duration, volume, location, time of day, jurisdiction, zone class, distance band, bill class, provide class, type of product, equipment class code, service code and many more attributes and combinations. It’s possible to have inputs in one unit and rating in different units. For each charge, minimum and per unit charges can be also defined. Amdocs Kenan also supports pre-rated usage to be re-rated or loaded without applying additional charges.
In normal invoice processing, discounts and allowance are applied on usage collected during the current bill run, regardless if it’s late or not. In such a case, a late call from a previous month will consume allowance of the current month. Amdocs Kenan also supports special late usage handling through configuration which allows late usage needs to be discounted based on the month it belongs to (event transaction date) and re-calculate related discounts applied to previous invoices. This means discount and allowance adjustments need to be provided for each discount reassessed. Notifications enable service providers to track spending across multiple thresholds and profiles, such as specific types of usage, specific products, and services or at the aggregated levels of the customer account or corporate hierarchy.
In Singtel perspective in Rating we have Usage preprocessor , Bulk meter , Multimedia , Resale, Usage Outpayment etc.
The Usage Preprocessor processes incoming CDRs (Call Detail Record) coming from various sources (i.e. CSI, Multi-media, Meter reading, etc.) to produce output CDRs in the Arbor/BP ST01 format. The Usage Preprocessor also processes rejected CDRs from the CSI splitter (stage 1 and 2), handle the usage that come later then X number of day.  Finally, the usage preprocessor also processes priced CDRs generated from CSI stage 3 rejections.  The generated usage file will be sent to Arbor/BP for further processing (guiding and rating). The UPP can reformat an incoming CDR of any format into one or more output CDRs in the ST01 format by using the following functionalities:
recognizing the input format based on an input field
moving input fields to corresponding fields in the ST01 format
filling ST01 fields with values, depending the values of certain fields in the input CDR
massaging the content of input fields depending on the value of other input fields and placing the result in an ST01 field
Set the completion status field to 5, if the transaction date of the incoming usage is older than X number of days.
splitting the output CDR into one or more CDRs and modifying the content of the duplicate CDRs based on values in the input or output CDR.
The UPP modules only provide the tools to perform these functionalities. When a functionality needs to be performed, on which input CDRs and with which values is all table driven and therefore depends on how the UPP is configured.
This document only provides a high-level description of what the UPP modules do. 
Bulk Meter processing
In Bulk Meter processing, there are cyclic reading process, DBMR extractor, exchange reading process, Bulk Meter preprocessing and absorption process.
There are new provide and ceased orders raised everyday.
These orders will be extracted in CSN list to Bulk Meter where the first job, DBMR extractor will extract readings from DBMR based on the service numbers and dates.
After this, the next job “exchange reading process” will update bi_prevreading based on the service numbers and their readings. There could be rejections such as a service number cannot be reprovisioned before it is ceased. These rejections will be updated into bi_report and a report will be sent to Billing Ops via another job.
When a service number is provided in bi_prevreading, it will be billed every week. This happens when the cyclic dump from switch exchange to CSI is passed down to Pegasus and updates the bi_prevreading. The difference in the reading between the cyclic dump and the provision record in bi_prevreading will be sent to Arbor via usage stream and billed accordingly.
About once in two years, the switch exchanges will be upgrading their switches and readings from old switches need to be billed off before the new switches are used.
The absorption module is built to cater for this purpose.
The absorption sort and validate process will check that each input record in the absorption file is in the correct format and any duplicates in the absorption file will be removed and not processed. The accepted records will then be sorted according to their service numbers. Each service number is expected to have one CMO and CMN record which means the old switch reading and new switch reading records.
The update of readings in bi_prevreading will take place via exchange reading process again.
Special Considerations:
 Guiding cyclic record 
The reading date in the Bulk Meter CDR file to Usage Preprocessor is subtracted by 1 to allow the usage to be guided to the correct customer when an SI transfer takes place on same day as cyclic dump.
For instance, service number 61234567 used by customer A is provisioned on 2 Feb 2003 and ceased on 10 Feb 2003. Customer B takes over the service number on 10 Feb 03. If the cyclic dump happens on 10 Feb, current program logic will set the reading date in the CDR file to 10 Feb as well. However, in Arbor, the end date for Customer A is 10 Feb 03 and Bulk Meter usage with reading date on 10 Feb will be guided to customer B that is provisioned on 10 Feb. This results in under-billing for customer A and over-billing for customer B. (see figure A)
If the reading date becomes 9 Feb 03 after subtraction, it will then be guided to the correct customer which is customer A. However, to maintain bill presentation consistency, the reading date before subtraction will be appended to the annotation of the CDR file. The BIF module will then take this date as the to_date in the bill presentation.
Customer A’s usage			Customer B’s usage
2 Feb						10 Feb
Figure A
For existing usage records without to_date in annotation field, BIF module will still be able to cater for them by checking for to_date in the annotation. If there is no to_date, BIF module will take trans_dt as to_date since there is no subtraction done on trans_dt for  usage records before the change.
GST Processing 
To take care of GST revision from 4% to 5%, there will be a TR (Tariff Revision) and cyclic records splitter where TR records will be sent to TR stream while cyclic records to cyclic stream. The purpose of processing TR records is to bill customers at 4% for usage up to 31 Dec 2003. Usage from 1 Jan 2004 onwards at 5% will then be taken care by processing cyclic records.
These TR records would come in with the date on 1 Jan 2004.  In order to compute the local usage before 2004 as 4%, the processed TR records that sent to usage stream (UPP) will be subtracted one day from the TR date which is 31 Dec 2003.  This is because Arbor will rate any usage record dated 1 Jan 2004 as 5% GST. The TR records will first be processed and bi_prevreading will be updated before continuing with the cyclic records.
In addition, CSI will still send TR record even after 1 Jan 2004 for any backdated provision order. Therefore, we need a TR stream to always cater for GST revision for these cases to prevent billing errors. Pls note that before any revision taking place such as on 1 Jan 2004, the S04 rejection checking should be switched off to prevent unnecessary rejections. This is because on 1 Jan 2004, both TR and CYC records send down to Pegasus will have the same date. Hence, it will result S04 rejection when come to CYC record processing after TR record processing.
Besides, E02 checking should be turned on just before 1 Jan 2004 to ensure all the expected TR records are found in the cyclic dump from CSI.
Both S04 and E02 checking can be controlled by setting them in the ini files of TR and cyclic processing jobs.
 Manual Upload
Sometimes, daily orders could have failed during exchange reading process due to no readings found for service numbers or numbers not being assigned in DBMR. This will usually cause the next order to be rejected.
For example, a FIN order is being rejected as W01 due to FIN reading not found for the service number. This service number is then added to the delay file and the search for the FIN reading would continue until the next day. However, if the next provision order comes in the following day, it will be rejected as E04 since the service number is not ceased yet. 
Billing Ops will then need to manual upload the provide record into bi_prevreading. Currently, the manual upload job only allows upload of INI and FIN records to bi_prevreading and a Bulk Meter cdr file will be sent to usage stream at the end of upload process. 
However, we must allow flexibility to upload CYC records into bi_prevreading as well as to have the option whether to send Bulk Meter cdr record to usage stream. At times, OP/OM team could have patched records in OP_CSN that are not extracted to bi_prevreading and we need to patch bi_prevreading accordingly. A more convenient and efficient approach is to allow flexibility of manual upload process to patch records in bi_prevreading without sending down any cdr record to usage for billing.
E02 Check
With five streams of processing jobs, the E02 check which is in processing job BIUBMC201W last time has to be in the new job BIUBMM201W.  This is because each processing stream has only a portion of the full dump and E02 check if carried here, will result in false E02 rejections. E02 check here refers to checking for any missing weekly records for any active number in bi_prevreading.
The new job BIUBMM201W after completion of the 5 streams run, will check for any records in bi_prevreading where proc_flag = N and reading type != FIN. This indicates a situation where weekly record did not come for an active number in bi_prevreading. After completion of BIUBMM201W, a control report will be sent to Actuate to reach Billing Ops for investigation.
Spare lines Recovery
Upon receiving the recovery file, BIURBM201O will need to check whether any of service lines with the Recovery Range is of Spare Status in bi_prevreading and OP_CSN during the Recovery date.
For records under Spare status, they will be archived and removed from bi_prevreading. As for records under Active status, they will be rejected, and records are inserted in bi_report under error code E09 for Billing Ops investigations.
Multimedia billing integration process
SingNet and Magix will be sending prerated charges to Pegasus for convergent billing. The charges will be sent to Pegasus in 3 files, 2 from SingNet and 1 from Magix. The first SingNet file contains itemized usage charges, the second contains RCs, NRCs, adjustments, summarized usage, unit credits and rebates. The Magix file only contains summarized usage. The purpose of the Multimedia billing integration process is to:
Validate the individual files and their content according to the validation rules.
Split the validated records into 2 groups depending on whether they should be uploaded via the usage preprocessor or via the NRC upload program.
Split the NRC upload records into 4 files depending on whether they are account or service instance level NRCs and depending on which customer server (1 or 2) the charges should be guided is to.
Reformat and modify the record to simplify the preprocessor configuration and the NRC upload program.
Produce an error file containing the erroneous records with an error description appended to each record.
Upload the charges through the preprocessor or through the NRC upload program.
Resale
With the launch of Pegasus Phase 2 and the migration of consumer customer data over into Pegasus, the full billing capabilities present in CSI will need to be emulated in Pegasus so as to allow a seamless transition for our customers from the old system to the new.
One such capability will be the handling of Resale Usage currently undertaken solely by CSI. Resale Usage means usage records that are received by SingTel Billing System but are not meant to be billed by SingTel to the end customers who had utilized that service. These usage records will instead be passed to the respective resale customers with SingTel taking a commission off of these resale usages.
The resale dumper module will extract the rated CDRs for the resale dummy service instances in CDR_DATA having external_id like ‘Resale Usage for xx’ and external_id_type is ‘10’ daily based on the rate_dt. The program will then copy these CDRs from CDR_DATA into BI_RESALE_CDR. 
After the CDRs have been copied into BI_RESALE_CDR, each of these CDRs will have its no_bill set to ‘1’ and cdr_status set back to ‘2’,‘3’ or ‘5’. This is done so that the records will not get picked up for billing accidentally or get extracted again into BI_RESALE_CDR in subsequent resale dumper runs.
There will be another 2 programs created for the purpose of extracting Resale usage to the External Operators and producing the reports required to mimic the current workflow in CSI. 
The requirement for the Resale usage extraction is to minimize impact to the External Operators by following existing file formats and reports as closely as possible.
The pre-extraction module will calculate and populate records in BI_RESALE_CDR with the information to be extracted by the Resale extraction module. The extraction module will then extract CDRs belonging to the relevant External operator from BI_RESALE_CDR into an output file and produce some reports to be sent together to the External Operator.
The usg_extract date field in BI_RESALE_CDR will be populated with the system date during the extraction job run when the CDRs are extracted and sent to the External Operators based on the agreed frequency. This is to prevent duplicate extractions.
For extractions that are weekly (currently StarHub), a monthly job will be scheduled on the 1st of the next month to extract all resale usage for that operator, which had not been extracted before, from the last weekly extraction to the end of the month.
Resale Traffic Types for extraction will include: 01, 06, 14, 15, 16 and 31.
BFDD’s for Resale usages.
Outpayment usage.
Calls made using the subscriber’s personal credit card via the Operator Assisted, or Manual Trunk Call – need to be extracted on weekly basis to UOB Bank and On-Demand system. This is needed in order for the bank, which is the clearing house for such transactions to pay Singtel weekly through the Giro system. The reports generated for the On Demand System is needed in order to enable customer’s queries on their credit card calls to be handled. Hard copy reports are also generated for Billing Operations for consolidation purposes.

Thresholding
Amdocs Kenan includes controls in the rating process. It is important to note that the time which is critical for some of the controls is dependent on the mediation solution that sends the EDRs to Amdocs Kenan.  
In response to the need for ever-tighter control of financial risk, Amdocs Kenan offers a “fast batch” rating process flow which converts unrated files from mediation to rated and accumulated events in the billing database. Within this flow, the charge accumulator provides the scope for a variety of types of intervention with the service end-user, though is primarily intended for enterprise customers who do not necessarily require split-second response times when unbilled spending thresholds are breached.
Advanced Rating – Thresholding module is a powerful solution for telecommunications operators, especially those with mobile and internet services, who require near real-time accumulation of usage charges for comparison against configurable threshold parameters. This module monitors any network usage against flexible parameters and offers multiple channels for acting when a threshold has been exceeded. Thresholding maximizes return on investment by ensuring end-users stay within the set usage boundaries, and it manages fraud risk by initiating actions whenever a customer's eligible outstanding usage exceeds predefined amounts. In addition, thresholding can be used to increase customer satisfaction and retention by triggering events that reward customers for their usage.  
Advanced Rating – Thresholding module keeps a running total of usage events for the billing product accounts and account components. Accumulation of usage data can be performed for any product of any service instance and for all accounts in any associated account hierarchy.
Accumulation provides an estimate of the unbilled usage charges within a hierarchy, account, service instance, product or usage type. The running totals are kept for rated amounts and for usage units. Totals can provide a picture of usage by account, service instance or product in an event-driven manner. This information is always available and can be used in conjunction with external systems, such as Interactive Voice Recognition (IVR), to provide up-to-date information to existing customers, thus decreasing incoming call volumes (This may require integration with specific IVR systems). By using provisioned threshold profiles, running totals can be used to initiate actions in various ways. 
Figure 25	Thresholding Actions
The Advanced Rating – Thresholding module tracks totals of usage, recurring charges, non-recurring charges and unit credits. For instance, operators can use alarms to notify customers who have exceeded threshold limits, to warn supervisors of fraud risks or to reward customers for their usage. It is possible to set multiple alarms, as well as act throughout the account hierarchy. These actions can also trigger the execution of a script and/or actions can be triggered in provisioning systems. For example, the operator could automatically terminate service for fraudulent or credit-risk customers (a provisioning system-specific integration would need to be in place for this action to be fully automated).

CICD team will build Bamboo deployment plan to sftp artifacts to target server and folder.
Post deployment of .sql Files in target application servers , release manager / CICD team will inform back the respective application team .

Batch Interfaces uses Secured File Transfer Protocol (SFTP) connection to transfer the files
All Batch Interface files are been archived automatically
Inbound
It moves data files from the R2 Billing’s  staging directory to the application                       destination directory (which is usually the central mount directory)
Inbound Get
It goes to the external system, get files, and put it in R2 Billing’s Interface staging directory
Outbound
It transfers outbound files from the R2 Billing’s staging directory to the external system.

    "Kenan Module List": "Billing
Singtel Billing includes the 26 Bill cycles in a month starting from 1st (Billing execution starts from 3rd of the month)  from every month to 26th/27th of the Month. We have 3 types of billing in Singtel in a day.
Cyclic Billing 
This is scheduled Bill cycles for the day like M01, C01, R01 etc. 
Non-Cyclic Billing 
Non-Cycle Billing includes the interim bills and fallout/catch up cases for previous Bill cycles.
Proforma Billing
Proforma Billing is to validate some test bills  before the final bill cycle.
Bill Processing
Bill processing comprises of stream of jobs. However, this document only focuses on four jobs:
BIP Initialization
Script for BIP Execution
Post BIP Error Detection Script
Script to dump BBCQ and BIU – before bill run
Script to dump BBCQ and BIU – after bill run
These four jobs are part of the Bill Cycle (Cyclic and Non-cyclic) Processing Stream. The flow is illustrated below:
The other jobs in the Bill Cycle Processing Stream will not be documented here. However, this document will address the guideline/standard of designing jobs to be run in the Bill Cycle Processing Stream.

Rating
Amdocs Kenan supports file-based offline rating for post-paid subscribers. The rating engine supports a sophisticated model based on customer and product offering characteristics as well as admitting in-line promotions and charge monitoring for notification purposes. The engine delivers high performance and supports diverse interpretations of chargeable events. 
The Message Processing System (MPS) calculates usage charges for customers (and in some cases for foreign accounts as well). MPS performs the following tasks
Batch Usage Processing Flow
Collects usage files from a network mediation layer.
Parses each file to determine the type, time, duration, and other properties of corresponding usage events. 
Guides each usage event to an Amdocs Kenan or external account. 
Rates each usage event and stores the usage charge and related information in the database.
Exports out collects (rated usage events for foreign carriers) and reseller usage events.
Usage can be rated based on duration, volume, location, time of day, jurisdiction, zone class, distance band, bill class, provide class, type of product, equipment class code, service code and many more attributes and combinations. It’s possible to have inputs in one unit and rating in different units. For each charge, minimum and per unit charges can be also defined. Amdocs Kenan also supports pre-rated usage to be re-rated or loaded without applying additional charges.
In normal invoice processing, discounts and allowance are applied on usage collected during the current bill run, regardless if it’s late or not. In such a case, a late call from a previous month will consume allowance of the current month. Amdocs Kenan also supports special late usage handling through configuration which allows late usage needs to be discounted based on the month it belongs to (event transaction date) and re-calculate related discounts applied to previous invoices. This means discount and allowance adjustments need to be provided for each discount reassessed. Notifications enable service providers to track spending across multiple thresholds and profiles, such as specific types of usage, specific products, and services or at the aggregated levels of the customer account or corporate hierarchy.
In Singtel perspective in Rating we have Usage preprocessor , Bulk meter , Multimedia , Resale, Usage Outpayment etc.
The Usage Preprocessor processes incoming CDRs (Call Detail Record) coming from various sources (i.e. CSI, Multi-media, Meter reading, etc.) to produce output CDRs in the Arbor/BP ST01 format. The Usage Preprocessor also processes rejected CDRs from the CSI splitter (stage 1 and 2), handle the usage that come later then X number of day.  Finally, the usage preprocessor also processes priced CDRs generated from CSI stage 3 rejections.  The generated usage file will be sent to Arbor/BP for further processing (guiding and rating). The UPP can reformat an incoming CDR of any format into one or more output CDRs in the ST01 format by using the following functionalities:
recognizing the input format based on an input field
moving input fields to corresponding fields in the ST01 format
filling ST01 fields with values, depending the values of certain fields in the input CDR
massaging the content of input fields depending on the value of other input fields and placing the result in an ST01 field
Set the completion status field to 5, if the transaction date of the incoming usage is older than X number of days.
splitting the output CDR into one or more CDRs and modifying the content of the duplicate CDRs based on values in the input or output CDR.
The UPP modules only provide the tools to perform these functionalities. When a functionality needs to be performed, on which input CDRs and with which values is all table driven and therefore depends on how the UPP is configured.
This document only provides a high-level description of what the UPP modules do. 
Bulk Meter processing
In Bulk Meter processing, there are cyclic reading process, DBMR extractor, exchange reading process, Bulk Meter preprocessing and absorption process.
There are new provide and ceased orders raised everyday.
These orders will be extracted in CSN list to Bulk Meter where the first job, DBMR extractor will extract readings from DBMR based on the service numbers and dates.
After this, the next job “exchange reading process” will update bi_prevreading based on the service numbers and their readings. There could be rejections such as a service number cannot be reprovisioned before it is ceased. These rejections will be updated into bi_report and a report will be sent to Billing Ops via another job.
When a service number is provided in bi_prevreading, it will be billed every week. This happens when the cyclic dump from switch exchange to CSI is passed down to Pegasus and updates the bi_prevreading. The difference in the reading between the cyclic dump and the provision record in bi_prevreading will be sent to Arbor via usage stream and billed accordingly.
About once in two years, the switch exchanges will be upgrading their switches and readings from old switches need to be billed off before the new switches are used.
The absorption module is built to cater for this purpose.
The absorption sort and validate process will check that each input record in the absorption file is in the correct format and any duplicates in the absorption file will be removed and not processed. The accepted records will then be sorted according to their service numbers. Each service number is expected to have one CMO and CMN record which means the old switch reading and new switch reading records.
The update of readings in bi_prevreading will take place via exchange reading process again.
Special Considerations:
 Guiding cyclic record 
The reading date in the Bulk Meter CDR file to Usage Preprocessor is subtracted by 1 to allow the usage to be guided to the correct customer when an SI transfer takes place on same day as cyclic dump.
For instance, service number 61234567 used by customer A is provisioned on 2 Feb 2003 and ceased on 10 Feb 2003. Customer B takes over the service number on 10 Feb 03. If the cyclic dump happens on 10 Feb, current program logic will set the reading date in the CDR file to 10 Feb as well. However, in Arbor, the end date for Customer A is 10 Feb 03 and Bulk Meter usage with reading date on 10 Feb will be guided to customer B that is provisioned on 10 Feb. This results in under-billing for customer A and over-billing for customer B. (see figure A)
If the reading date becomes 9 Feb 03 after subtraction, it will then be guided to the correct customer which is customer A. However, to maintain bill presentation consistency, the reading date before subtraction will be appended to the annotation of the CDR file. The BIF module will then take this date as the to_date in the bill presentation.

For existing usage records without to_date in annotation field, BIF module will still be able to cater for them by checking for to_date in the annotation. If there is no to_date, BIF module will take trans_dt as to_date since there is no subtraction done on trans_dt for  usage records before the change.
GST Processing 
To take care of GST revision from 4% to 5%, there will be a TR (Tariff Revision) and cyclic records splitter where TR records will be sent to TR stream while cyclic records to cyclic stream. The purpose of processing TR records is to bill customers at 4% for usage up to 31 Dec 2003. Usage from 1 Jan 2004 onwards at 5% will then be taken care by processing cyclic records.
These TR records would come in with the date on 1 Jan 2004.  In order to compute the local usage before 2004 as 4%, the processed TR records that sent to usage stream (UPP) will be subtracted one day from the TR date which is 31 Dec 2003.  This is because Arbor will rate any usage record dated 1 Jan 2004 as 5% GST. The TR records will first be processed and bi_prevreading will be updated before continuing with the cyclic records.
In addition, CSI will still send TR record even after 1 Jan 2004 for any backdated provision order. Therefore, we need a TR stream to always cater for GST revision for these cases to prevent billing errors. Pls note that before any revision taking place such as on 1 Jan 2004, the S04 rejection checking should be switched off to prevent unnecessary rejections. This is because on 1 Jan 2004, both TR and CYC records send down to Pegasus will have the same date. Hence, it will result S04 rejection when come to CYC record processing after TR record processing.
Besides, E02 checking should be turned on just before 1 Jan 2004 to ensure all the expected TR records are found in the cyclic dump from CSI.
Both S04 and E02 checking can be controlled by setting them in the ini files of TR and cyclic processing jobs.
 Manual Upload
Sometimes, daily orders could have failed during exchange reading process due to no readings found for service numbers or numbers not being assigned in DBMR. This will usually cause the next order to be rejected.
For example, a FIN order is being rejected as W01 due to FIN reading not found for the service number. This service number is then added to the delay file and the search for the FIN reading would continue until the next day. However, if the next provision order comes in the following day, it will be rejected as E04 since the service number is not ceased yet. 
Billing Ops will then need to manual upload the provide record into bi_prevreading. Currently, the manual upload job only allows upload of INI and FIN records to bi_prevreading and a Bulk Meter cdr file will be sent to usage stream at the end of upload process. 
However, we must allow flexibility to upload CYC records into bi_prevreading as well as to have the option whether to send Bulk Meter cdr record to usage stream. At times, OP/OM team could have patched records in OP_CSN that are not extracted to bi_prevreading and we need to patch bi_prevreading accordingly. A more convenient and efficient approach is to allow flexibility of manual upload process to patch records in bi_prevreading without sending down any cdr record to usage for billing.
E02 Check
With five streams of processing jobs, the E02 check which is in processing job BIUBMC201W last time has to be in the new job BIUBMM201W.  This is because each processing stream has only a portion of the full dump and E02 check if carried here, will result in false E02 rejections. E02 check here refers to checking for any missing weekly records for any active number in bi_prevreading.
The new job BIUBMM201W after completion of the 5 streams run, will check for any records in bi_prevreading where proc_flag = N and reading type != FIN. This indicates a situation where weekly record did not come for an active number in bi_prevreading. After completion of BIUBMM201W, a control report will be sent to Actuate to reach Billing Ops for investigation.
Spare lines Recovery
Upon receiving the recovery file, BIURBM201O will need to check whether any of service lines with the Recovery Range is of Spare Status in bi_prevreading and OP_CSN during the Recovery date.
For records under Spare status, they will be archived and removed from bi_prevreading. As for records under Active status, they will be rejected, and records are inserted in bi_report under error code E09 for Billing Ops investigations.
Multimedia billing integration process
SingNet and Magix will be sending prerated charges to Pegasus for convergent billing. The charges will be sent to Pegasus in 3 files, 2 from SingNet and 1 from Magix. The first SingNet file contains itemized usage charges, the second contains RCs, NRCs, adjustments, summarized usage, unit credits and rebates. The Magix file only contains summarized usage. The purpose of the Multimedia billing integration process is to:
Validate the individual files and their content according to the validation rules.
Split the validated records into 2 groups depending on whether they should be uploaded via the usage preprocessor or via the NRC upload program.
Split the NRC upload records into 4 files depending on whether they are account or service instance level NRCs and depending on which customer server (1 or 2) the charges should be guided is to.
Reformat and modify the record to simplify the preprocessor configuration and the NRC upload program.
Produce an error file containing the erroneous records with an error description appended to each record.
Upload the charges through the preprocessor or through the NRC upload program.
Resale
With the launch of Pegasus Phase 2 and the migration of consumer customer data over into Pegasus, the full billing capabilities present in CSI will need to be emulated in Pegasus so as to allow a seamless transition for our customers from the old system to the new.
One such capability will be the handling of Resale Usage currently undertaken solely by CSI. Resale Usage means usage records that are received by SingTel Billing System but are not meant to be billed by SingTel to the end customers who had utilized that service. These usage records will instead be passed to the respective resale customers with SingTel taking a commission off of these resale usages.
The resale dumper module will extract the rated CDRs for the resale dummy service instances in CDR_DATA having external_id like ‘Resale Usage for xx’ and external_id_type is ‘10’ daily based on the rate_dt. The program will then copy these CDRs from CDR_DATA into BI_RESALE_CDR. 
After the CDRs have been copied into BI_RESALE_CDR, each of these CDRs will have its no_bill set to ‘1’ and cdr_status set back to ‘2’,‘3’ or ‘5’. This is done so that the records will not get picked up for billing accidentally or get extracted again into BI_RESALE_CDR in subsequent resale dumper runs.
There will be another 2 programs created for the purpose of extracting Resale usage to the External Operators and producing the reports required to mimic the current workflow in CSI. 
The requirement for the Resale usage extraction is to minimize impact to the External Operators by following existing file formats and reports as closely as possible.
The pre-extraction module will calculate and populate records in BI_RESALE_CDR with the information to be extracted by the Resale extraction module. The extraction module will then extract CDRs belonging to the relevant External operator from BI_RESALE_CDR into an output file and produce some reports to be sent together to the External Operator.
The usg_extract date field in BI_RESALE_CDR will be populated with the system date during the extraction job run when the CDRs are extracted and sent to the External Operators based on the agreed frequency. This is to prevent duplicate extractions.
For extractions that are weekly (currently StarHub), a monthly job will be scheduled on the 1st of the next month to extract all resale usage for that operator, which had not been extracted before, from the last weekly extraction to the end of the month.
Resale Traffic Types for extraction will include: 01, 06, 14, 15, 16 and 31.
